#2170. TMW: Amorim asks for a right-sided defender – Feyenoord star the No.1 target

AC Milan are looking for a right-sided defender ahead of the January window, and a new target has popped up: Givairo Read.

Milan are currently without Samuel Chukwueze and Alexis Saelemaekers due to injury, while Pervis Estupinan and Davide Bartesaghi don’t seem to have fully convinced Ruben Amorim yet. So, there has been talk of the pursuit of a wide player.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As a result of this, TMW confirm that Milan are looking for a right-back even as early as the winter window. The latest name on the Rossoneri’s radar is Givairo Read, who is a star for Feyenoord and now for Xavi Hernandez’s Netherlands side.

Scouts will continue to monitor him during this international break, but they have already seen him up close. The 20-year-old made headlines in Italy when he marked and successfully stopped the in-form Rafael Leao in a match against Milan, in which Feyenoord knocked the Diavolo out.

Read was closely followed by Roma last summer. The Giallorossi attempted to lure him away from the Rotterdam club after Zeki Celik left for Juventus. The club’s attention then turned elsewhere, with Nahuel Molina chosen as the full-back.

Last summer, Inter also considered him as a replacement for Denzel Dumfries. However, Milan are now the main suitors, also because Fikayo Tomori – who has been used on the right side of the defence so far – remains set to leave before 2027-28.

Amorim himself has requested a reinforcement in the role and Read is seen as attractive because of his potential, but also for the immediate contribution he could make. Feyenoord must be convinced, and they might not sell for less than €30m.

#2169. Napoli su Sebastiano Esposito: Giuffredi faciliterebbe l'operazione, Manna prova ad accelerare

Giovanni Manna, ds del Napoli, avrebbe individuato in Sebastiano Esposito, attaccante attualmente al Sassuolo, un possibile rinforzo per la squadra di Massimiliano Allegri già per il mercato di gennaio. La dirigenza azzurra avrebbe già avviato i primi contatti con il club neroverde per verificare la fattibilità dell'operazione e individuare una formula che possa soddisfare tutti.

Secondo quanto riferito da Radio Kiss Kiss Napoli, un ruolo importante nell'eventuale trasferimento potrebbe essere ricoperto da Mario Giuffredi, agente dell'attaccante e procuratore di diversi calciatori azzurri, tra cui Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Matteo Politano, Antonio Vergara e Costantino Favasuli. I rapporti consolidati tra Giuffredi e la società di Aurelio De Laurentiis agevolerebbero di molto l'arrivo dell'attaccante in azzurro. L'obiettivo sarebbe ora trovare un'intesa già nelle prossime settimane per portare il talento stabiese a Napoli.

Lo stesso Giuffredi negli scorsi giorni aveva pubblicizzato un possibile tridente con Hojlund e Vergara: "Si incastrerebbero benissimo, perché Sebastiano è un toro a livello fisico. Vergara ha grande forza nelle gambe. Hanno anche colpi tecnici, sono imprevedibili. Non sarebbe male".

#2168. Clamoroso: l'UEFA pensa all'ex Inter per sfidare Infantino alla presidenza FIFA. Ma spunta un rivale

Clamoroso: l'UEFA pensa all'ex Inter per sfidare Infantino alla presidenza FIFA. Ma spunta un rivale

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

A tre giorni dalla scadenza per le candidature alla presidenza della FIFA, la UEFA è ancora alla ricerca del candidato che sfiderà Gianni Infantino. Dopo aver preso in considerazione Sandor Csányi, presidente della Federazione calcistica ungherese, e poi Arsène Wenger, che alla fine si è ritirato, i vertici europei stanno ora valutando una nuova opzione.

Secondo le fonti del portale Footmercato, diversi funzionari della UEFA stanno attualmente promuovendo internamente l'ex Inter Luis Figo. L'ex nazionale portoghese, che aveva già tentato di candidarsi alla presidenza della FIFA nel 2015 prima di ritirarsi, non è tuttavia una scelta unanime all'interno della UEFA. Le discussioni proseguiranno quindi negli ultimi giorni prima della scadenza.

La posta in gioco è alta per l'organo di governo del calcio europeo, che spera di presentare una candidatura congiunta contro Gianni Infantino, che cerca un quarto mandato dopo aver assunto la guida della FIFA nel 2016. L'elezione si terrà il 18 marzo 2027 a Rabat, in Marocco, durante il Congresso FIFA. Per essere ufficialmente selezionato, ogni candidato deve ottenere il sostegno di almeno cinque federazioni affiliate alla FIFA. I candidati hanno tempo fino al 18 novembre per presentare la propria candidatura. La UEFA ha quindi pochissimo tempo per raggiungere un accordo e stabilire se Luis Figo riuscirà a ottenere il consenso dei suoi vertici.

#2167. Bonera believes Milan Futuro were not ready for first season: “Some thought it was easier”

Daniele Bonera has revisited his time as the head coach of Milan Futuro, revealing his belief that the team wasn’t ready to compete.

The Futuro project was launched ahead of the 2024-25 season to give Milan a ‘second team’ to allow their young talents to develop at a level above that of the Primavera league. They started in Serie C but were relegated in their first season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was taken to sack Bonera as the head coach given the on-field issues, even though they were competing against experienced sides with a very young side. Massimo Oddo followed him, before the club chose to go with Sergio Navarro this summer, who has the Futuro in third.

Bonera was interviewed by Fanpage and he reflected on that period with the B-team and what he learned from it even despite the rough results, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan Futuro was a great opportunity for growth. Perhaps we weren’t clear – and I’m part of this – about the level of Serie C. I had an idea of ​​it, but some thought it was easier,” he said.

“The squad had been built with expectations that were too high compared to what the league is. I don’t think that structure, at that time, was ready to tackle that type of league. On an individual level, however, I felt very comfortable. Starting at home was a positive thing.

“The biggest challenge was understanding which players you actually had available. Some were promoted to the first team, others were dropped, and still others were sent to the Primavera. We had guys who perhaps weren’t playing with us and then came back up.

“From an individual growth perspective, we worked very well in some situations. After a couple of years, we saw the individual value of guys like Camarda, Bartesaghi, Liberali, and Jimenez grow. The value of the players wasn’t in question.

“I think the problem was primarily structural: it’s not always the coach who’s the problem, but the way you do things and the direction you want to take.”

Quando l’Inter tornerà a giocare a San Siro, mercoledì 25 in Champions contro lo Stoccarda, troverà un nuovo terreno di gioco (che sarà già testato dal Milan domenica contro il Frosinone).

Come scrive Tuttosport, infatti, "dopo Italia-Francia di giovedì, è infatti iniziato un intervento completo di rizollatura del campo.

Un rinnovato articolato, coordinato da tecnici specializzati, sviluppato in quattro fasi: la rimozione completa dello strato superficiale vegetale usurato (detto “scotico”, svolto venerdì); livellamento millimetrico e preparazione del sottofondo per accogliere il nuovo manto (sabato); posa delle nuove zolle (da sabato a domani); cucitura del manto e rinforzo sintetico per completare il sistema ibrido del terreno di gioco (da mercoledì a sabato prossimo)".

#2164. Avellino, il sindaco Pizza sul nuovo stadio: "Vogliamo realizzarlo, ma attendiamo la Regione"

Il futuro del Partenio-Lombardi resta al centro dell'attenzione ad Avellino. Il sindaco Nello Pizza è tornato sull'argomento, invitando la piazza a mantenere calma e serenità e ribadendo la volontà dell'amministrazione comunale di realizzare un nuovo impianto. Restano però da definire le modalità dell'intervento e il coinvolgimento dei soggetti interessati.

"Questa amministrazione ha dichiarato espressamente di voler fare il nuovo stadio. Ora stiamo valutando come realizzarlo. Se potremo farlo con D'Agostino saremo contenti di farlo con lui; in alternativa valuteremo se farlo con un altro imprenditore o se finanziarlo interamente noi", ha spiegato Pizza. Il primo cittadino ha poi sottolineato la vicinanza del Comune all'US Avellino, assicurando che verrà fatto tutto il possibile per portare avanti il progetto.

Sul fronte economico, il sindaco ha però richiamato alla necessità di rispettare procedure e tempi, trattandosi di un investimento con risorse pubbliche. "I soldi che investiremo non sono nostri personali, ma sono soldi pubblici, quindi bisogna fare attenzione e rispettare le procedure senza subire pressioni da nessuno".

Un passaggio fondamentale sarà quello relativo ai finanziamenti regionali: secondo Pizza, infatti, il Comune non dispone di risorse proprie da destinare all'opera e sarà necessario attendere la Regione, indicata come l'unico soggetto in grado di finanziare il progetto. Lo riporta Tuttoavellino.it

#2162. “Didn’t forget how to play football” – Füllkrug reflects on time away from Germany including Milan spell

Niclas Füllkrug has again looked back on his time at AC Milan, joking that he ‘didn’t forget how to play football’.

Füllkrug joined Milan midway through the 2025-26 season on loan from West Ham and it was hoped that he could boost their Scudetto hopes, if not at least get them over the line in the top four battle. However, he scored just once and ultimately was not bought permanently.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The German headed back to Werder Bremen in the summer, and has been in remarkable form since. He has scored nine goals in the Bundesliga which makes him the top scorer, and 13 goals in 11 games across all competitions, at an average of one every 64 minutes.

As a result, he was called up by coach Jurgen Klopp for the final two UEFA Nations League group stage matches against Serbia and the Netherlands. Speaking at a press conference, he revisited his short stint with the Diavolo.

“I was never unhappy during my time abroad. I’m very grateful for those experiences because there’s so much more to life than football. Of course, football is very important, but when you live abroad, you can still separate your personal life from your professional one,” he said (via MilanNews).

“I took away many positive memories from those two years. The main problem was that I struggled to stay in shape. I didn’t forget how to play football during that time.”

Con la Nazionale verdeoro conquistò il Mondiale nel 1958, mentre con i rossoneri vinse la Coppa dei Campioni nel 1963. A dare la notizia è stata la Federcalcio brasiliana, attraverso una nota ufficiale. "Abbiamo perso uno dei nostri primi campioni del mondo. Questo il comunicato di saluto del Milan: "Il Milan perde un pezzo della sua storia. Dino Sani, protagonista degli anni '60 rossoneri: uno Scudetto, una Coppa dei Campioni, 78 partite e 20 gol con la nostra maglia. Dino Sani ha contribuito a cambiare un'intera epoca del Milan, lasciando un'impronta che il tempo non cancellerà. Alla sua famiglia e ai suoi cari l'abbraccio commosso del popolo rossonero. Ciao Dino, e grazie per aver fatto grande il Milan".

#2157. Reports: Spurs and Juventus call Milan as on-loan midfielder continues to shine

AC Milan made the decision to loan Youssouf Fofana out in the summer window, and he is attracting interest from clubs around Europe.

Fofana’s situation ended up being quite a dramatic one. He was excluded from the plans by Ruben Amorim and seemed set to join Lyon on loan, but that fell through on deadline day. A move to Turkey didn’t materialise, but Sevilla stepped forward and managed to get a year-long loan deal done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since moving to Spain, Fofana has found his best form again. Having played nine LaLiga games for the Andalusian side so far, he has four goal contributions to his name, with one goal and three assists.

Calciomercato.com cite TEAMtalk and Spanish sources, who claim Fofana is attracting the interest of clubs like Tottenham and Juventus. They have already initiated preliminary discussions with Milan to assess the feasibility of a deal for next summer.

The club coached by Roberto De Zerbi has reportedly made concrete moves, beginning initial dialogue with Milan management, while Juve were linked in the summer and are still looking for midfield reinforcements.

For their part, Milan remain interested in listening to any offers that may arrive, considering that Amorim is still firmly in charge and has already expressed his opinion that the Frenchman is not a fit for his style and system.

The Rossoneri value the midfielder at around €15m, according to reports from abroad, and are waiting for interested clubs to make more concrete moves ahead of next season.

Sevilla meanwhile would not be able to pay the cost of the player’s wages, but would like to negotiate with Milan to extend their relationship with Fofana beyond this one-year loan, attempting to set up a permanent deal next summer.

#2155. Chi è Leon Scarlett, l'astro nascente del calcio gallese finito nel mirino del Milan

Leon Scarlett è uno dei giovani talenti emergenti del calcio inglese. Nato il 16 agosto 2009, ha compiuto 17 anni ed è cresciuto nel settore giovanile dell'Arsenal, prima di trasferirsi al Queens Park Rangers nel gennaio 2025, quando ha firmato un accordo di formazione con il club londinese. Il suo percorso è stato particolarmente rapido: dopo aver attraversato le selezioni giovanili, ha iniziato ad allenarsi con la prima squadra, conquistando le prime opportunità in Championship. Nel complesso, ha già collezionato sei presenze complessive nella seconda divisione inglese, cinque delle quali nell'attuale stagione.

Il suo ruolo è quello di esterno offensivo, con la possibilità di agire sia sulla fascia destra sia su quella sinistra. La duttilità rappresenta una delle caratteristiche più interessanti del suo profilo, insieme alla capacità di adattarsi a diverse posizioni del reparto avanzato. Scarlett ha inoltre scelto di rappresentare il Galles a livello internazionale: dopo le esperienze con le selezioni giovanili, è stato convocato anche dalla Under 21 per le qualificazioni agli Europei del 2027, un traguardo significativo considerando la sua età.

La crescita del diciassettenne non è passata inosservata. Milan ed Eintracht Francoforte hanno manifestato non a caso interesse per il giocatore e continuano a seguirne l'evoluzione. Non si parla ancora di offerte o trattative concrete: entrambe le società stanno monitorando la situazione. Per Scarlett, intanto, la priorità resta trovare continuità al QPR e proseguire un percorso che potrebbe portarlo presto sotto i riflettori del grande calcio europeo.

#2154. MN: Allegri expressed ‘annoyance’ over Milan’s €8m deal for Cisse – the reasons

Alphadjo Cisse is the man of the moment for AC Milan, and yet there were some within the club at the time who opposed his arrival.

Cisse is currently the top scorer in the team with eight goals to his name, earning him a senior Italian national team call-up from Roberto Mancini. All this for a player who missed the first half of 2026 due to injury and has only just turned 20.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is now talk of Premier League clubs expressing their interest in signing him, but in the meantime Milan have a counter-move ready: the extension of his contract with a pay rise as a reward.

MilanNews reveal the back story regarding his arrival. In January, Cisse seemed destined to join PSV Eindhoven, but a phone call from Milan changed everything. When the Rossoneri entered the race, the forward put PSV on hold and made it clear where he wanted to go.

Milan then convinced Verona with a bid of €8m and persuaded Cisse with a development plan, including that he could remain on loan in Serie B with Catanzaro. Geoffrey Moncada identified him and Giorgio Furlani was key in the negotiations with his agency CAA Base, too.

However, not everyone at Milan was in favour. The report claims that Massimiliano Allegri did not like the idea of allocating part of the budget on a young player while his side were in a title fight. Niclas Füllkrug was the only first-team reinforcement, arriving on loan from West Ham.

Allegri did not fail to express his ‘annoyance and negativity’ regarding the Cisse operation, which was later finalised by Furlani. In the end, the head coach, CEO and the chief scout (Moncada) would all be dismissed after the final game of the season.

#2153. Bristol City must eye ex-Premier League boss if they sack Michael Skubala: Opinion

Bristol City managed to lure the 44-year-old away from Lincoln City in the summer on a three-year deal after he guided the Imps to the League One title. However, he has struggled to adapt to life in the Championship and his side’s recent form hasn’t been great.

The Robins are reportedly sizing up potential replacements as they aim to rise up the table. With that in mind, they should target a move for Steve Cooper if they decide to part ways with Skubala in the near future.

Cooper, 46, is available following his exit from Brondby back in May and he will be weighing up his next move in the game. He has recently been linked with Derby County amid uncertainty over John Eustace’s position, whilst his name was also in the frame for the Burnley job back in June following their relegation from the Premier League.

The Welshman would be ideal for Bristol City and he knows the EFL inside out. They are currently positioned in 17th place in the table after 15 fixtures.

Bristol City will have aspirations of reaching the top flight in the coming years. They have great facilities and a big catchment area.

However, the Robins haven’t been able to get it right yet and need someone like Cooper to lead them forward. He knows what it takes to get out of the second tier after guiding Nottingham Forest up back in 2022.

Prior to his switch to the City Ground, he got Swansea City into the play-offs as well. The Pontypridd-born man is a proven performer at Bristol City and landing him would be a big statement of intent.

Cooper’s more recent spells at Leicester City and Brondby haven’t quite gone to plan. Therefore, he will have a point to prove now and the Robins can provide him with a platform to show what he can do again and give him an exciting project to lead.

Bristol City supporters are becoming increasingly frustrated and the heat is on Skubala after their 5-0 home loss to Norwich City last time out. They are back in action on Saturday away at Middlesbrough.

If the Robins’ hierarchy plan to dismiss Skubala, they would have probably done it during this international break. It appears they are sticking with him for now.

If they do sack him eventually, Cooper should be top of their list of replacements. Other available names consist of Steven Gerrard, Sean Dyche, Rob Edwards and Paul Heckingbottom.

#2151. Malagò torna sulla rinuncia di Galliani: "Scelta di buon senso, ma eviti polemiche pretestuose"

Dopo le dichiarazioni rilasciate a margine della 35ª edizione della Panchina d’Oro, il commissario straordinario della FIGC, Giovanni Malagò, è tornato a commentare, con una nota stampa, la decisione di Adriano Galliani di rinunciare al ricorso contro l’ammissione della sua candidatura: “Giovanni Malagò accoglie favorevolmente la decisione del Sen. Adriano Galliani di non impugnare il provvedimento di ammissione della sua candidatura alla Presidenza federale.

Una scelta di buon senso, perché un’ulteriore iniziativa contenziosa avrebbe soltanto alimentato tensioni delle quali il calcio italiano non ha alcun bisogno, senza offrire alcun contributo al confronto sui programmi e sul futuro della Federazione. Già la contestazione relativa alla nomina della Commissione, sollevata senza neppure richiedere un chiarimento che sarebbe stato semplice fornire, ha generato inutili allarmismi in un clima fin troppo teso, certamente non per iniziativa di Giovanni Malagò.

Il richiamo alla responsabilità e alla serenità del percorso elettorale è dunque apprezzato e condivisibile. La coerenza con questi obiettivi si misura, però, anzitutto nella capacità di evitare polemiche ed iniziative pretestuose, non soltanto nella rinuncia a darvi ulteriore seguito. Giovanni Malagò continuerà a privilegiare il confronto sui contenuti e il dialogo con tutte le componenti del sistema, nell’interesse del calcio italiano”.

Il riferimento di quest'ultimo passaggio è con tutta probabilità legato alla nota con cui il senatore di Forza Italia ha annunciato la rinuncia all'impugnazione, facendo riferimento a un "pericoloso precedente" costituito dalla doppia firma del Genoa.

#2150. Moretto: ‘Cardinale likes him a lot’ – Tresoldi interest confirmed but Milan face difficult pursuit

Matteo Moretto has provided an update on AC Milan’s pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi, confirming the concrete interest.

Tresoldi’s rise to stardom is one that has naturally seen him enter Milan’s orbit, given that he is a publicly declared boyhood fan of the club. After an impressive start to the campaign with Club Brugge, it was his hat-trick in the Champions League against Inter at San Siro that made many take note.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The rumours have since followed linking him with what would be a ‘dream’ move to the Rossoneri, in his father’s words. La Gazzetta dello Sport spoke this morning of a €50m January attempt being lined up by Gerry Cardinale, to give Goncalo Ramos an attacking partner.

Speaking in a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Moretto shed some light on where things are currently at regarding the future of Tresoldi, and MilanNews transcribed what he had to say.

“A few days ago I told you how Milan were really close to signing Tresoldi a few years ago, so much so that the boy arrived, visited Milanello and was at Casa Milan, the contracts were even ready,” he began.

“I want to clarify that, since he was a very young boy at the time, it was not an operation directly supervised by Paolo Maldini. There were other people who were managing that operation. At the time, Ricky Massara was also Milan’s transfer manager and there were other people as well.

“The operation actually never got to the point because Milan stalled and the player returned to Germany, effectively signing a new contract with Hannover. Beyond this, there is now a lot of talk about Tresoldi in terms of Milan’s present and future.

“However, I want to clarify a few points. I can confirm that it is true that Cardinale likes him a lot and Milan likes him a lot. The club is evaluating what kind of steps to take to attempt this type of coup, but there are several points to clarify.

“First of all, the position of Club Brugge, Because Club Brugge are a very difficult club to deal with. We also need to understand Club Brugge’s results in the Champions League, because if they advance to the next round, they will earn a lot of money and won’t need to sell.

“Club Brugge’s idea is to keep Tresoldi until the end of the season to finish their season well. Regarding the money Club Brugge is asking for, we need to see if €50m will be enough.

“These are important points, and then there’s a lot of competition in Europe, because several clubs in Spain, Germany, and England are interested in Tresoldi. AC Milan are interested, and it’s true that AC Milan are looking for a striker in January.”

#2149. Middlesbrough and Will Lankshear’s stance on January transfer as further interest emerges

Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear has put himself in the spotlight with stunning form since moving to Teesside in a £20m package deal. The Boro man has 15 goals in 16 games across all competitions, and has already been the subject of transfer speculation with Newcastle United said to be keen.

Now, a report from TEAMtalk details further interest. They claim that all of Manchester United, Brighton & Hove Albion, Everton, Sunderland and Borussia Dortmund have all scouted Lankshear, while North London rivals and former clubs Spurs and Arsenal are both monitoring the situation as well.

However, Boro have no desire to sell Lankshear, and the 21-year-old is not looking for a swift step up either. The Championship’s top scorer is ‘delighted’ with his progress and focused on maintaining his form as Kim Hellberg‘s side push for promotion to the Premier League.

There’s a lot of hype around Lankshear’s future and excitement over what the coming years could have in store. It’s understandable too, as it isn’t every day that a 21-year-old English striker averages a goal every 78 minutes for a Championship club.

But, for now, it is of paramount importance that Lankshear is allowed to focus on his football as he continues to progress his game. Harry Kane – who the Middlesbrough star has already been compared to – has urged patience regarding his emergence and development.

Moving up to a Premier League club would bring increased pressure and scrutiny for Lankshear while he is still progressing. Stepping to a higher level too soon could actually stunt his growth.

While he is in flying form and playing regularly, Lankshear is in the ideal place for his progression. Boro are on the up themselves as they challenge for Championship promotion as well, so it could be that he makes the rise on Teesside.

Although Middlesbrough have no intention of cashing in and Lankshear won’t be pushing for a move, that doesn’t mean that interest will ease up. Clubs are sure to keep monitoring his situation and tracking his performances given his high ceiling and impressive form.

Their stances may well change the plans of any admirers who were planning a winter approach. However, it seems that those who do make moves will either be told that Lankshear is not available at any price, or they will be given a sky-high valuation to fend off further interest.

Lankshear seems bound for the top, but there should be no rush to get there. He can make the rise in good time, but only if the developmental years of his career are managed correctly.

#2148. GdS: Four exclusions, four defeats – Milan’s Pulisic dependance highlighted

There are many ways to outline Christian Pulisic’s importance to AC Milan, but one of them is very simple: wins.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have outlined the fact that when Pulisic starts a match, Milan do not lose. In an inconsistent team like Ruben Amorim’s, the four defeats this season to Benfica, Bournemouth, Bologna and Ferencvaros have two things in common.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the two starters in midfield: four times out of four, the double pivot was Yunus Musah and Ardon Jashari each time. Then, there are the three absentees: Mario Gila, Luka Modric and Pulisic.

Pulisic, Gila and Modric are clearly three of Milan’s key players, and the American arguably more so than the others. He’s eighth in Serie A in points average from starts (2.67 points, five wins in six games).

Pio Esposito, Lulli, Mora (the three who have always won as starters), Zaccagni, Dimarco, Isaksen, and Zielinski rank higher, but there’s a clear difference: the others play for Lazio, Inter, and Roma, the top three in the league.

Captain America came on against Benfica, Bologna, and Ferencvaros, and was an unused substitute against Bournemouth. Compared to Modric, who has been playing consistently since August, and Gila, who has been affected by injury, Pulisic has had his ups and downs.

He scored in Udine, the derby and most recently against Genoa, and it’s no coincidence that the Diavolo won all three games. Simply put: when Christian plays well, Milan follow him. When his level drops, Milan struggle.

It’s tactics, as well as numbers. Pulisic has different characteristics from his team-mates: he’s the only one who attacks the space in behind. Gonçalo Ramos often comes deep and lays it off, Alphadjo Cisse loves having the ball at his feet, and CP disrupts defences in other ways.

Furthermore, he’s considered one of the owners’ key players, who are also American, and he just renewed his contract. If you have to imagine the Milan of the future, just think Pulisic and 10 others.

#2147. Foggia, il ds Casella: "Il mercato non è una priorità, pensiamo a prestazioni e classifica"

La sconfitta nel derby contro il Bari lascia il Foggia con tanti rimpianti e la necessità di cambiare passo. Il 3-2 del San Nicola ha evidenziato alcune fragilità della squadra rossonera, sulle quali il direttore sportivo Alex Casella ha chiesto di intervenire. Nonostante la delusione, il dirigente ha ribadito la propria fiducia nel gruppo, invitando tutti a una maggiore responsabilità.

"C'è rammarico, soprattutto quando parti in quel modo. Per leggerezza abbiamo concesso dei gol e siamo una squadra che non può permettersi queste disattenzioni. Dobbiamo saper gestire meglio la partita e migliorare nella lettura delle situazioni", ha dichiarato in sala stampa, come riportato da Foggiacalciomania.com.

Casella ha poi allontanato l'attenzione dal mercato, sottolineando come in questo momento la priorità debba essere il rendimento sul campo. "Siamo a novembre ed è sbagliato concentrarci sul mercato. In futuro si lavorerà, ma adesso dobbiamo focalizzarci sulle prestazioni, sulle partite e sulla classifica".

Il direttore sportivo ha infine condiviso le responsabilità con tutto l'ambiente rossonero, chiamando in causa anche l'allenatore e chiedendo un confronto per individuare gli aspetti da migliorare. "In qualsiasi momento della stagione mi sento responsabile, ma non sono solo io: lo siamo tutti. Dobbiamo confrontarci insieme, anche con il mister. Bisogna intervenire su tante cose, alzare l'asticella. Questo gruppo può farlo".

#2144. Birmingham City pair may now regret summer transfer moves to the Blues: Opinion

Birmingham City delved into the European market to lure the pair over to England in the last transfer window. However, neither have been able to make the impact they would have wanted to at BCFC so far this season.

Lund, 24, was brought in after the Blues sold Kai Wagner back to Philadelphia Union and he has struggled to get into Chris Davies’ starting XI due to strong competition from the in-form Alex Cochrane. He has been limited to only three appearances in all competitions since his move, two of which have come in the Championship.

As for Vazquez, 25, he hasn’t been able to find his shooting boots and has failed to score in 14 outings altogether. The striker, who penned a contract running until June 2029, is down the pecking order behind August Priske is his position and faces a serious battle for game time.

Birmingham City are sat top of the Championship table above Middlesbrough and Stoke City on goal difference so you can understand why Davies is reluctant to change a winning team. They beat Swansea City 2-1 at home before the international break.

Birmingham City signed Lund to boost their defensive department. BCFC head coach Davies doesn’t seem to fancy him though and much prefers Cochrane.

Prior to his switch to the Blues, he had a loan spell at FC Koln in the Bundesliga. He put pen-to-paper on a long-term deal running until 2030 so he still has plenty of time to turn things around at St Andrew’s and force his way into the picture.

Vazquez provides cover for Priske but his confidence will be low at the moment. The ex-Boca Juniors man missed an open net against Derby County back in mid-September.

The former Argentina youth international desperately need to find the net but the longer his goal drought goes on, the more pressure he will be under to perform. He spent time on loan at Getafe last term in La Liga from Anderlecht before his previous team sold him permanently.

Birmingham City seem unlikely to offload Lund in January, despite his lack of minutes. If Cochrane picked up an injury, he would be needed by BCFC.

It wouldn’t be a surprise to see the Blues consider Vazquez’s future though. His transfer hasn’t worked out and if the price is right or a loan opportunity arises, they may be tempted to cut ties.

Davies would benefit from another attacker this winter and if they were able to get someone else in, they could do with freeing some space and funds by letting Vazquez depart. Birmingham City are back in action this weekend away at Stoke City.

#2143. Tra i migliori in campo a Bruxelles, Ngoy piace da tempo al Milan. Il prezzo si alza ancora

Il Milan lo segue da tempo, ma la prestazione di ieri a Bruxelles rischia di complicare i piani dei rossoneri. Nathan Ngoy, difensore classe 2003 del Lille, è stato tra i migliori in campo nel 4-1 con cui il Belgio ha battuto l'Italia di Roberto Mancini. Suo il gol del momentaneo 2-1, arrivato al 22' dopo una respinta di Donnarumma sul colpo di testa di Mechele. Una rete che è stata, tabellino alla mano, quella della vittoria.

Ventitré anni compiuti a giugno, Ngoy è arrivato al Lille nell'estate del 2025, dopo essere cresciuto tra Anderlecht e Standard Liegi. In Francia ha trovato la continuità che gli era mancata nelle stagioni precedenti, anche a causa di diversi problemi fisici. Difensore centrale di piede destro, utilizzabile anche sulla fascia, ha caratteristiche che possono tornare utili sia in una linea a quattro sia in una difesa a tre come quella di Ruben Amorim.Il Milan ne segue da tempo la crescita, ma non è l'unico club interessato: anche in Premier League il suo nome è stato accostato a diverse società.

Il problema, per i rossoneri, rischia di essere economico. Il Lille ha Ngoy sotto contratto fino al 2029 e non ha necessità di cederlo a condizioni particolarmente favorevoli. Se fino a qualche mese fa la sua valutazione si aggirava intorno ai 25 milioni di euro, in Belgio si parla già della possibilità che il prezzo raggiunga quota 40 milioni nella prossima estate. Non è una richiesta ufficiale del club francese, ma una stima legata alla crescita del giocatore. Una cifra che renderebbe decisamente più complicata un'eventuale operazione del Milan, soprattutto considerando la concorrenza inglese.

Roma are ahead of AC Milan in the race to sign Endrick from Real Madrid, but things can change before the winter window.

Milan have been heavily linked with a move for Endrick since the summer window, when they pursued the 20-year-old before ultimately turning to Omari Hutchinson after Jose Mourinho blocked any chance of an exit for the Brazilian.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The rumours have not gone away as January approaches – instead they have only intensified. This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport bizarrely suggested that Endrick wants Roma over Milan for religious reasons, though these claims are yet to be verified.

In a video published on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Matteo Moretto spoke about Milan’s pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi. He also touched on the situation at Real Madrid regarding Endrick, with his words via MilanNews.

“Although Mourinho continues to say that Endrick will stay at Real Madrid, the truth is that the player has the ball at the moment. If the player decides to tell Real Madrid that he wants to try a new experience to grow and play, Real Madrid will not object. And I can tell you that these are precisely the indications,” he said.

“To date, there have been no official communications between the parties, but I can confirm that Endrick, as he also stated in a recent interview, is open to a new loan experience, Lyon-style, which could give him that extra spotlight and playing time, also with a view to the national team. Endrick wants to play.

“I’m telling you that there are two clubs in Italy right now, but Roma is the club that’s ahead. Roma has always maintained contact, they’re after the player, and they watched him very closely in that famous Champions League match won by Real Madrid right in the dying minutes.

“I know that Endrick currently has a better chance of leaving than staying. Roma is quite far ahead, while Milan are slightly behind, despite the good relations between Cardinale, Roc Nation, and between Milan and Real Madrid. There are Premier League and Portuguese clubs interested in Endrick.”

#2140. Sheffield Wednesday need to strike permanent deal for 29-year-old in the January transfer window: Opinion

Sheffield Wednesday landed the attacker on a temporary basis in September on a short-term deal. He has since made a positive impression at Hillsborough and has become one of SWFC’s main players so far this season in League One.

Keillor-Dunn, 29, has made 12 appearances for the Owls in all competitions to date, 10 of which have come in the league, and he has chipped in with six goals and one assist. The South Yorkshire outfit need to pursue a permanent move for him this winter and he can flourish under the guidance of new head coach Dave Challinor over the coming months.

The Sunderland-born man is a proven performer at third tier level and was a shrewd addition. Wrexham gave him the green light to head out the exit door to get some more game time under his belt and he hasn’t looked back.

Sheffield Wednesday won 3-0 at home against Plymouth Argyle last time after goals by Keillor-Dunn, Billy Mitchell and Di’Shon Bernard and they have risen back into the play-offs. The Owls are back in action on Friday night with an away trip to Barnsley.

Sheffield Wednesday’s decision to bring in Keillor-Dunn has worked out well for them. He injects valuable quality into SWFC’s starting XI.

He knows where the back of the net is and causes problems for opposition defenders. When everyone is available, he battles it out with the likes of Mason Burstow, Jamal Lowe and Ali Al-Hamadi for a place in the Owls’ team.

Keillor-Dunn re-signed for Wrexham back last February after six years away and penned a contract until June 2029 in North Wales. However, he has since found it hard for minutes at the Racecourse Ground, hence why they let him leave.

He is unlikely to ever break into the Red Dragons’ team due to strong competition for places in his position. Therefore, they will surely be tempted to cash in on him if Sheffield Wednesday can match his valuation.

Sheffield Wednesday manager Challinor will be eager to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad in January with some additions. SWFC already have a player in Keillor-Dunn who is performing so securing his future has to be a no-brainer.

The Owls are eyeing promotion to the Championship at the first time of asking this term. They were relegated earlier this year after finishing in the bottom three along with Leicester City and Oxford United.

#2139. Barcellona, tegola Cubarsí: sovraccarico all'ileopsoas, è in dubbio per il Villarreal

Il Barcellona perde momentaneamente certezze in difesa. Pau Cubarsí ha accusato infatti un problema muscolare al rientro dagli impegni con la nazionale spagnola e il club catalano ha pubblicato un aggiornamento sulle sue condizioni. Gli esami hanno evidenziato un sovraccarico al muscolo ileopsoas, il gruppo muscolare che collega la zona lombare e il bacino al femore e che svolge un ruolo importante nei movimenti dell'anca. Non si tratta, almeno secondo il comunicato blaugrana, di una lesione muscolare grave.

Il classe 2007 aveva accusato un fastidio all'anca durante la partita tra Spagna e Inghilterra, terminata 3-2 per gli inglesi. Per questo motivo Luis de la Fuente aveva deciso di sostituirlo all'intervallo, inserendo Dean Huijsen al suo posto. Una scelta precauzionale che aveva inizialmente fatto temere un problema più serio, prima degli accertamenti effettuati a Barcellona.

Adesso l'attenzione si sposta sulla prossima partita contro il Villarreal, in programma domenica 22 novembre. Hansi Flick spera di recuperare il proprio difensore, diventato un elemento fondamentale della retroguardia blaugrana. Il club catalano non ha comunicato tempi di recupero precisi: sarà l'evoluzione del sovraccarico nei prossimi giorni a stabilire se Cubarsí potrà tornare a disposizione oppure dovrà saltare l'appuntamento di Liga.

#2136. Liverpool plan on loaning out 13-goal starlet in January – QPR should consider a move: Opinion

QPR had a fairly quiet summer transfer window but recruited well. Their six signings saw key areas addressed, improving in goal with Pierce Charles and Calum Ward while depth was added at full-back with Boy Kemper, Dennis Cirkin and Tariq Lamptey signing.

The Hoops sit 8th in the Championship table after 15 games, so they’re in the play-offs conversation. January will be key in deciding whether they remain in the hunt or slide into mid-table.

There aren’t glaring areas of the squad that require improvement, but the frontline was untouched in the summer, and there is a case to be made for upgrading. One player who could breathe new life into QPR’s striker department is Liverpool prospect Will Wright.

The Daily Mail has reported that Liverpool are planning a January loan move away for 18-year-old hotshot Will Wright. The Anfield outfit signed him from Salford City in 2025 and he has quickly become one of their standout youth players.

Wright has 13 goals and three assists in 12 games for Liverpool’s U21s this season, starring in the Premier League 2 and UEFA Youth League. Standing at 193cm tall, he can hold up play and win the ball in aerial duels, but he is deceptively quick and isn’t afraid to carry the ball with mazy runs either.

And, as would be expected of someone with his youth goal record, Wright knows how to put the ball in the back of the net too.

Liverpool feel he needs to develop physically against stronger opponents, and he will certainly get that in the Championship. QPR could be a good place for him to do so, as they have a goalkeeper in Charles who will be able to pick out Wright with long balls into the channels, or onto his chest or into his feet.

Furthermore, the existing physical forwards like Richard Kone means the onus won’t be solely on Wright to be the target man. He’ll get exposure to tough physical duels without having the responsibility of seeing to this task all alone.

The R’s have created 37 big chances this season – the 10th most in the Championship – so Wright will get goalscoring opportunities with his smart movement. And, given his finishing instincts, he’d be backed to net a few goals.

The question for QPR will be whether Wright is an upgrade on what they already have. In Kone, Rumarn Burrell, Rayan Kolli and Justin Obikwu, Stephan has enough depth to go without a striker signing; especially considering Paul Smyth and Alfie Lloyd can play there too.

But, Wright has shown more promise than Obikwu, who could benefit from a loan of his own. Furthermore, there has been past uncertainty over Kolli’s situation, while Kone and Burrell have had injuries.

Wright could be a necessary reinforcement and an upgrade on the existing depth. He could perform well in the Hoops’ setup and would get the physical test Liverpool desire as they plot the next steps for one of their most exciting prospects.

#2135. Mancini sbaglia partita, De Bruyne fa a pezzi l’Italia. A Napoli è colpa di Allegri? Milan, ecco Krosche che vuole lo scudetto con Tresoldi e Inacio. Tre giovani per Napoli: Varela, Bakola e Cacciamani. Juve punta Sorloth e Balde

Pesante ritorno sulla terra per l’Italia che soffre il Belgio come e più di quanto successo nella gara d’andata. Una disfatta difficile da accettare dopo la partita perfetta contro la Francia, ma facile da spiegare. Il Belgio è più forte di noi e si sapeva, il dominio è stato totale. E’ il loro gioco ad alta velocità con grande tecnica che ci mette in crisi, il movimento frenetico, le rotazioni con cambi di posizione, gli esterni che spingono, senza un centravanti vero, il pressing costante, gli azzurri non c'hanno capito niente, non hanno mai trovato gli avversari perdendo le posizioni e tutti i duelli. Una sconfitta che è pure figlia di alcune scelte di Mancini difficilmente comprensibili come Pisilli centrocampista messo a presidiare la zona destra, o il lento Fagioli opposto a giocatori molto veloci, non era la sua partita. Nel primo tempo gli azzurri non l’hanno mai vista. Ma anche Koleosho è andato in difficoltà nella fase difensiva. Una sconfitta che però non può spazzare via tutto quello che di buono s’è visto in questo Mancini-bis, con la consapevolezza che la strada sarà ancora lunga prima di trovare equilibrio e personalità compiute. Mancini che, fra l’altro, potrebbe tornare in discussione se Malagò dovesse perdere le elezioni del quattordici dicembre, ributtando tutto nel caos. Speriamo di no.

In attesa, dobbiamo sottolineare l’ennesima grande partita di De Bruyne, assoluto dominatore di tutte le partite della sua nazionale. E allora come si spiegano le sue prestazioni insufficienti e le sue difficoltà a prendere in mano il Napoli?

E’ molto probabile che il belga non gradisca il tipo di calcio passivo proposto da Allegri, soffra il grande lavoro che gli viene chiesto nella fase difensiva. La squadra non gli gira attorno, non si diverte e così perde gran parte della sua enorme qualità e il sorriso. Una riflessione andrebbe fatta, anche se alla fine è probabile che il giocatore finisca al Psv Eindhoven già a gennaio facendo risparmiare sei milioni netti alle casse del Napoli. Sarebbe una sconfitta per tutti non essere riusciti a godere del suo enorme talento. Ma del Napoli riparleremo più avanti.

Dopo la nazionale, riecco il campionato con tutte le problematiche e il mercato di gennaio alla porta. La grande svolta probabilmente arriverà da Cardinale che s’è messo in testa di vincere lo scudetto, quindi ha pronti gli acquisti per sistemare i punti deboli del Milan. Il budget c’è, il nuovo capo dell’area tecnica pure. Come sappiamo, anche se arriverà ufficialmente solo a gennaio, è già operativo il tedesco Markus Krosche, 46 anni, ex Eintracht Francoforte. In Germania ha fatto benissimo, ha sistemi innovativi di valutazione, con una grande rete di scouting. Per gennaio gli obiettivi sono tre, un centravanti dal gol facile, un difensore centrale e un esterno destro di difesa.

Può arrivare Tresoldi? Sarebbe un grande colpo per il Milan, ma anche in chiave nazionale. Il ragazzo, 22 anni, ha sempre tifato i rossoneri. Venire in Italia potrebbe anche convincerlo a scegliere la nazionale azzurra come auspicato da Mancini. Il problema, ovviamente, è il Brugge. La squadra belga chiede una cifra attorno ai sessanta milioni e c’è da verificare la possibilità di trattare già per il mese di gennaio. Su tutto questo stanno lavorando Cardinale e Krosche tenendo aperta anche la porta con il Real Madrid per il brasiliano Endrick, 20 anni.

In questo caso sarebbe una operazione diversa, un prestito con qualche clausola. Il problema è Mourinho che non vuole mai mollare i giocatori anche se li utilizza pochissimo come Endrick. Il ragazzino preme, l’anno scorso a gennaio era stato prestato e vorrebbe una soluzione analoga. In corsa c’è pure la Roma, ma Cardinale da tempo ha aperto un canale con Florentino Perez.

Per il centrale, Amorim ha fatto da tempo il nome del suo preferito: Goncalo Inacio, centrale dello Sporting Lisbona, 25 anni. E’ un difensore dai piedi buoni, capace di guidare la difesa e fare ripartire l’azione, quello che serve al Milan. La valutazione supera i trenta milioni, ma il problema più grosso sembra la resistenza dello Sporting che (per ora) non lo vuole mollare a gennaio. Il filo però non s’è interrotto. L’alternativa è un profilo diverso, Luca Reggiani, 18 anni, strappato dal Borussia Dortmund al Sassuolo. Nazionale under 21, con i tedeschi ha già esordito in prima squadra.

Pensando al futuro, Krosche ha messo pure i riflettori anche su Stiller, regista dello Stoccarda, 25 anni, che ha una clausola da quaranta milioni. Potrebbe essere lui il dopo-Modric. Per il terzo ruolo scoperto, l’esterno destro, è probabile il ritorno anticipato di Athekame, 21 anni, in prestito al Lione dove sta facendo molto bene.

Almeno due anche gli obiettivi della Juve, un attaccante che la metta dentro, come si dice brutalmente, e un esterno sinistro dopo l’ennesimo flop di Cambiaso. Quest’ultimo ruolo potrebbe essere coperto da Aleandro Balde, 23 anni, che nel Barcellona sta trovando poco spazio. La valutazione è molto alta, attorno ai quaranta milioni. Il discorso è aperto. Ma in Spagna la Juve guarda sempre a Sorloth e sta parlando con l’Atletico mettendo sul tavolo la posizione di David che ha soddisfatto Simeone. Sorloth è un uomo d’area, vede la porta al contrario di Waltemade e con lo spostamento di Kolo Muani sulla destra, per caratteristiche sarebbe adattissimo a risolvere il problema vero della Juve: fare gol. Si pensa anche a Scamacca che Carnevali ha avuto al Sassuolo, i dubbi sono sulle sue frequenti ricadute fisiche.

Ma a gennaio si cercherà anche di sfoltire la rosa per recuperare risorse e snellire il lavoro di Spalletti che soprattutto davanti ha una batteria di trequartisti-esterni. Fra l’altro Ildiz dovrebbe rientrare al massimo a inizio anno, quindi gente come Zhegrova potrebbe andare in prestito, ma non solo lui. Oltre a Cambiaso potrebbe partire pure Kelly, ormai finito dietro a Gatti nelle gerarchie spallettiane.

E il Napoli? Inizia la rivoluzione verde. De Laurentiis ha dato via libera a Manna, la rosa va ringiovanita e sfoltita. Inoltre lo spogliatoio andrà liberato di tutti i casi che hanno complicato questo inizio stagione. Non sarà facile trovare una collocazione, ma la lista dei partenti è lunga, da Lucca a Lang, da Beukema a Anguissa che non vuole rinnovare, fino a Neres e Giovane. Manna le proverà tutte per arrivare ai tre giocatori giovani che ha nel mirino, vale a dire Varela, 21 anni, bomber del Monza, Bakola centrocampista del Sassuolo, 19 anni, e Cacciamani esterno del Toro, 19 anni. Varela ha segnato nove gol in dieci partite, il Monza l‘ha pagato due milioni e mezzo dal Benfica e la tentazione di monetizzare subito è forte. La richiesta supera i trenta milioni, ma il rischio di un’altra operazione Piatek frena parecchio gli operatori. Meglio aspettare giugno? L’interrogativo è logico, ma niente è deciso. Difficile, fra l’altro, che Lucca possa eventualmente accettare il prestito al Monza.

Il francese Bakola è stato pagato dieci milioni dal Sassuolo che l’ha strappato al Marsiglia. Ora per venderlo ne servono almeno trenta e c’è pure la concorrenza della Juve che ha (ovviamente) buoni rapporti con la società neroverde. I bianconeri lo vorrebbero acquistare subito per poi lasciarlo a Sassuolo fino a giugno. Alessio Cacciamani è un esterno sinistro tutta fascia. Il Torino chiede venti milioni, è interessata anche la Roma. Anche per questo ragazzo ogni discorso potrebbe essere spostato verso giugno, mentre Allegri ha chiesto rinforzi subito per provare a rimettere in moto il Napoli. Ci riuscirà? De Laurentiis, ovviamente, è deluso dal suo allenatore, ora si aspetta nove punti nelle prossime gare contro Torino, Sassuolo e Lecce. L’allenatore non è in bilico, ma in discussione. Queste tre partite sono una sorta di test, il presidente vuole una reazione forte e ovviamente la vittoria. Se si dovessero riproporre situazioni simili a quelle con il Venezia e altre, allora Allegri potrebbe davvero rischiare un altro esonero nonostante l’ingaggio, il licenziamento costerebbe infatti una cifra-monstre tra i venticinque e i trenta milioni.

#2134. Theo Hernandez meets Paolo Maldini and reportedly Ibrahimovic too in Milan return

Theo Hernandez has been back in Italy during the international break, meeting two of his former colleagues at AC Milan.

Theo first of all got Milan fans talking by posting a photo on his Instagram alongside club legend Paolo Maldini, presumably in Milan. It’s no secret that the French full-back saw the legendary defender as an idol and a role model.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The caption from the Frenchman was simple but telling: “Respect and admiration, always.” In the replies were comments from figures such as Rafael Leao (who wrote ‘I’m coming’) as well as Alessandro Florenzi and Kyle Walker.

A post shared by T H E O H E R N Á N D E Z (@theo3hernandez)

Meanwhile, AllMilan.it (via Goal) are reporting that Zlatan Ibrahimovic met Theo and his family in the city too. Their bond dates back to their years together with the Rossoneri between 2020 and 2022.

They shared the journey to Milan’s 2021-22 Serie A title and forged an important partnership in the dressing room and on the pitch. The defender has described his relationship with the Swede as very close on several occasions.

He has also said more than once that he and his wife Zoe hold the city of Milano close to their hearts. However, for now there are no concrete signs of talks over a possible return to Milan, but rather a chance to meet old friends during the break.

#2133. Crawley Town set to complete free transfer swoop for 31-year-old

Crawley Town are a side in trouble this season. They sit bottom of League Two and are still without a permanent manager after appointing Kevin Blackwell on an interim basis nearly a month ago.

The Red Dragons have not played a League Two game in November but have lost back-to-back cup matches, including an FA Cup upset away at Wimborne Town. Former Sunderland goalkeeper Vito Mannone was in goal for that fixture as they lost 2-0.

Now though, Ben Jacobs states Crawley Town are set to take action by signing free agent shot-stopper Dejan Iliev. The 31-year-old was last on the books of Romanian club Rapid Bucharest.

The EFL’s bottom side have three games in hand on Rochdale in 22nd. However, they sit six points adrift of safety and uncertainty remains over their managerial position with Colin Kazim-Richards yet to be permanently replaced.

Alongside the reported arrival of Iliev, Crawley Town have recently made two other free agent swoops. Experienced striker Connor Wickham has joined the side, as well as English midfielder Ayman Benarous.

The Red Devils have scored 13 goals so far this season, with only Exeter City and Northampton Town netting less frequently. Midfielder Dylan Morgan has been a standout performer netting five goals, but current No. 9 Danilo Orsi has only netted twice in the league.

Wickham joins in the hope he can provide a focal point up front for his side. The 33-year-old is known for his physical and aerial ability and brings experience to his new club.

Benarous is more youthful at 23, but he offers a decent amount of experience from his spells at Bristol City and Plymouth Argyle. He is a reliable player in possession and can cover on the left-hand side alongside his usual central midfield role.

Crawley Town currently have three goalkeepers, all of whom have featured more than once in the league this season. Iliev would be a fourth option, and potentially the strongest.

Nicolas Michalski is currently on loan from Blackburn Rovers, and Jackson Izquierdo signed from Crystal Palace in the summer. Izquierdo has played the least of the three goalkeepers, so perhaps a loan away awaits as he bids to develop.

Mannone has featured six times in League Two for Crawley Town this season. However, like the other goalkeepers, he has failed to make the position his own.

Dejan Iliev has only played three senior matches in English football, with Shrewsbury Town. However, it is hoped that his top-flight experience in European football will help him adapt to League Two well and become the starting shot-stopper at Broadfield Stadium.

#2131. GdS: The ‘dream’ and two alternatives – Milan draw up three-man centre-back wish list

AC Milan are in the market for a new central defender ahead of the winter window, and three names are on the list.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), Gerry Cardinale wants to give Ruben Amorim at least two signings in January. One of them will be a centre-forward – with Nicolo Tresoldi the ambitious idea at the moment – while the other will be a defender.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With Matteo Gabbia sidelined until well into January and Fikayo Tomori currently injured, Amorim has been juggling an emergency in recent weeks. It was a situation further compounded by an issue that arose for Strahinja Pavlović last week.

Fortunately for Amorim, he has found a capable alternative in the youngster Sankhoun Diawara. Looking ahead, however, the club is considering an addition that could immediately boost the level of the department.

A summer target was Gonçalo Inácio whom Amorim knows well, having coached him for years at Sporting CP. Dialogue with the Lisbon club has continued even during the current period when the transfer window is closed, following the failure to reach an agreement before.

Milan could renew their pursuit soon, though there is currently no consensus regarding his asking price. Furthermore, Inácio is left-footed and has primarily played as an outside centre-back throughout his career.

What the Rossoneri need right now is more of a right-footed player capable of rotating between a wide centre-back role and a central position. While it is true that Gonçalo adapted to the right side under Amorim, there are other candidates who are a more natural fit for that role.

For instance, Ismaelo Ganiou of RC Lens has been on the radar for some time. His contract renewal in August does not necessarily rule out a transfer, although there has been no further contact with the French club since initial discussions in the summer.

Among the new names, 21-year-old Massiré Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise is an intriguing prospect. The Belgian club have also moved quickly to secure their young star with a new contract until 2031. That said, it is not a major obstacle, and the price is around €15m.

#2130. Napoli, Lorenzo Lucca è costato 35,9 milioni. Rasmus Hojlund 44 oltre a 6 di prestito

Lorenzo Lucca è costato 35,9 milioni di euro al Napoli. Una cifra molto alta per chi è stato bocciato dopo pochi mesi da Antonio Conte, con il suo destino che sembra riprodursi quest'anno dopo il prestito - non buono - al Nottingham Forest.

Il centravanti della nazionale danese è stato pagato, in totale, circa 50 milioni. Al contrario di Lucca, una spesa relativamente corretta rispetto a quelle che erano le aspettative di rendimento. Nella lista dei prestiti ci sono poi Alisson Santos, 3,5 milioni per il periodo tra gennaio e giugno - non poco se non fosse stato poi riscattato - ma anche Elmas, 3,1 milioni. Il totale per i soli titoli temporanei è di 12,85 milioni di euro.

Nella lista si possono vedere anche le cifre di Sam Beukema, 30 milioni, e Noa Lang, 27. Due che non hanno esattamente sfondato in questo anno e mezzo di esperienza napoletana. Non poco nemmeno Milinkovic Savic, 21 milioni per chi non è ancora un titolare fisso della formazione di Massimiliano Allegri. 18,6 per Miguel Gutierrez, ma anche 16,8 per Alisson Santos che porta l'ammontare a 20,3. E poi c'è Giovane: 2 milioni di euro. Perché così poco? Come anticipato qui l'ammontare in realtà è da 20.

#2129. Quote prossima squadra Tresoldi, gennaio può riservare sorprese

Tra i giovani talenti più interessanti del panorama calcistico internazionale c’è sicuramente Nicolò Tresoldi. L'attaccante italo-tedesco sta vivendo una stagione da assoluto protagonista con la maglia del Bruges, come testimoniano numeri di grande impatto: 8 gol nelle prime 11 giornate di campionato, 5 nelle prime 4 gare di Champions League e 10 reti in altrettante partite di qualificazione all'Europeo con la Germania U21.

Prestazioni che non sono passate inosservate e che hanno inevitabilmente attirato l'attenzione dei principali club europei, con Milan e Roma in prima fila tra le società italiane interessate. La pista rossonera è particolarmente suggestiva: Tresoldi non ha mai nascosto la propria fede milanista e le recenti aperture di Gerry Cardinale a nuovi rinforzi per gennaio alimentano le voci di mercato. Non a caso, le quote Milan prossima squadra Tresoldi iniziano a suscitare particolare interesse.

Il Milan fa sul serio per Nicolò Tresoldi. Il club rossonero è al lavoro per regalarsi un nuovo centravanti a gennaio e l'attaccante del Brugge è in cima alla lista. L'investimento da oltre 70 milioni per Ramos, almeno finora, non ha risolto il problema del gol: da qui la necessità di intervenire con un profilo capace di garantire concretezza e continuità.

La valutazione di Tresoldi dovrebbe aggirarsi intorno ai 50 milioni di euro, cifra che il Milan considera un investimento strategico anche in prospettiva. L'intenzione è anticipare la concorrenza già nella sessione invernale, ma la trattativa resta legata alla disponibilità del Brugge ad aprire al dialogo senza alzare ulteriormente le proprie pretese.

La Roma ci aveva provato prima del Milan e potrebbe tornare alla carica per Nicolò Tresoldi già a gennaio. #2128. Tuttosport: Milan rekindle interest in Bologna star amid feeling of regret

AC Milan still retain an interest in signing Juan Miranda after being linked with him in previous years, a report claims.

Tuttosport write this morning that Miranda is establishing himself as one of the best specialists in his position in Europe. The numbers speak for themselves: he’s already provided six assists in the first part of the season.

No one in Serie A has more than that, and his creativity was seen first hand in Bologna’s comeback win at San Siro. Naturally, his performances have not gone unnoticed in Italy and England. The first inquiries are beginning to arrive, with a contract situation that is worth keeping an eye on.

The paper writes that Miranda is also appreciated by Milan, although the Rossoneri are kicking themselves a bit too. They had an agreement to sign him on a free transfer two years ago and then decided to walk away. In hindsight, it looks like a big mistake.

Bologna seized the transfer opportunity in the summer of 2024, and are now enjoying his exploits. At the same time, however, concern is beginning to mount given that his deal with the Rossoblu expires in just 19 months.

This is why the Bologna management have been trying to establish talks regarding a contract extension in the past few weeks. The work so far hasn’t led to great progress, and so the possibility of a sale to avoid losing the Spaniard in a cut-price deal (or even for free) may be evaluated.

Juventus are in the running too, and an immediate attempt to bring him to Continassa and give Luciano Spalletti the left-back he’s coveted since last summer can’t be ruled out. This is especially true if the Bianconeri are in contention for a top-four finish.

Beware of the Palladino effect: since the coach took over at Bologna, the Rossoblu have been soaring (17 points in seven games). If the Emilian side were to also be involved in the fight for a European spot, it would be more difficult to pry Miranda from them.

#2127. £2m West Brom loanee getting what he needs in League One loan – but one glaring issue remains

West Brom signed Alfie Gilchrist from Chelsea in a deal worth up to £2m in the summer of 2025. He enjoyed a positive spell on loan at Sheffield United in the 2024/25 campaign, so there was hope that the promising defender could become a valuable asset for WBA.

However, a tough debut campaign resulted in Gilchrist dropping down the pecking order. As such, the 22-year-old was sent out on loan to Leyton Orient for the 2026/27 campaign, giving him a chance to play regularly in his preferred role as a centre-back.

Gilchrist has found the game time he needed in his strongest position, and he’s earned praise for his performances too. However, there are some glaring weaknesses that will worry those back at The Hawthorns.

Gilchrist made his first two Leyton Orient appearances off the bench before a spell out through injury. It meant he had to wait until October 10th for his full League One debut, and the West Brom loanee has not relinquished his starting berth since.

In the last five third-tier games, Gilchrist has helped keep five clean sheets with Orient winning two, losing two and drawing one. He also played the full 90 minutes in the 5-1 FA Cup win over Harborough Town earlier this month.

With Gilchrist on the pitch, the O’s have conceded 0.53 goals per 90. He has averaged 12.27 defensive contributions per game, along with 9.07 clearances as well.

However, at WBA, there were worries over whether Gilchrist had the physical and aerial presence to deal with powerful Championship forwards. He’s a committed defender, but in terms of winning duels, his struggles have continued out on loan.

Gilchrist is averaging a duel success rate of 53.8% with 3.74 won per 90, ranking him in the bottom 18% and 10% of League One centre-backs (all stats via FotMob). The Baggies loanee has shown his ability in one-on-one defending, but when it comes to winning physical battles, he continues to struggle.

From his breakthrough at Chelsea, everyone knows Gilchrist has strong potential as a defender. He’s old-fashioned in the way that he likes to get stuck in and shows no hesitation in clearing the ball to guard his box.

However, when the game is as physical as it is now, teams need dominance in duels from their centre-backs. Gilchrist could not offer this at West Brom, and it is a weak part of his game at Leyton Orient as well.

It will raise questions over whether Gilchrist can cement a place at centre-back at WBA in the future. Perhaps his defensive ability will see him adapt to a full-back role in time, but if he wants to play at the heart of defence, he seems unlikely to do so in James Morrison’s 4-4-2 setup at Championship level.

Gilchrist will strive to improve in this area though. His mentality and commitment to defending means he can still progress into a fine centre-back, but questions will persist over his chances of doing so at The Hawthorns or in the Championship.

#2124. Top 15 best home fans in the EFL ranked

Throughout the English football pyramid lies the age-old debate: where can you find the best atmosphere at a football stadium in the country?

Many will argue that it is hard to make such a case that clubs in the Premier League provide such hostilities due to various factors which have recently influenced the matchday experience of supporters within the top-flight.

As such, to go in search of the answer to said question, football fanatics may have to dig deeper into the Championship, League One and League Two.

In all three divisions you will find old-school grounds, passionate fanbases and some of the country's biggest fallen giants, who are still able to attract strong crowds despite dwindling recent fortunes.

Football League World recently put forward the 15 clubs with the best sets of away supporters, and now the roles have been reversed, and we are now looking at which of the EFL's 72 sides have the best home fans.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

Getting this list underway are Cardiff City, who, in recent times, have been able to retain a strong core of loyal supporters in South Wales despite mixed on-pitch fortunes.

Indeed, only two clubs averaged a greater home gate than the Bluebirds' 19,564 last season during their promotion-winning campaign in League One, which is a testament to such loyalties when some visiting sides will have not brought the greatest of visiting crowds from across the English border.

That cross-nation rivalry often makes for a hostile atmosphere that can certainly be an advantage to Brian Barry-Murphy's side.

Next up are Leicester City, with Foxes supporters certainly seeing their loyalties tested at present, with the Russell Martin era not exactly getting off to the smoothest start following back-to-back relegations.

The locals in this part of the East Midlands still showed up with the second-highest average attendance in last season's Championship in fairness, although there have been question marks over the atmosphere generated in LE2.

That said, when the club's day-to-day running has been eye-catching for all the wrong reasons of late, emphasised by a six-point deduction in February, it isn't hard to see why the mood isn't great.

West Bromwich Albion are known for having one of the most loyal Championship fanbases, despite the fact the Baggies are competing against several local sides for a new generation of support.

Average attendance figures at The Hawthorns have been above a 20,000 figure ever since the beginning of the 2001/02 season, meaning the majority of the 26,804-capacity stadium has been full.

However, it has, again, been debated whether the atmosphere can be improved in B71 despite such an impressive level of core support.

In 12th are Bradford City, with the West Yorkshire side consistently drawing impressive attendance figures to Valley Parade season-on-season despite the fact the club has languished in the EFL's bottom two divisions since 2004.

The 2025/26 League One season saw Bantams fans average gates of 20,444, which was the second-strongest in the third tier, and with the club's owners doing their utmost to make season tickets affordable in this part of the world, even more seats have been taken up this term.

It was announced in pre-season that at least 16,352 season tickets had been sold for 2026/27 - a club record.

Plymouth Argyle fans are some of the most respected in the country, as they turn up in their thousands irrespective of the Green Army's fortunes on the pitch, whilst also making Home Park a notoriously difficult ground for visiting teams to take points away from.

Although the distances for those in the away end to travel can often put off visiting fans, there is still a strong atmosphere generated in this part of the world more often than not, and average attendances have, in recent seasons, stayed at a level between 15,000 and 16,000 - one of the strongest in the EFL's lower reaches

Sheffield United's home crowd at Bramall Lane make it into 10th on this list, with the stadium famed for generating a vociferous atmosphere on occasions, particularly from the Kop stand.

However, compared to many other sides who ranked high based on average attendances last season, it will have been a disappointment among Blades fans that almost 6,000 of the stadium's seats were not filled.

The current situation the club finds itself in at board level has also made for an intriguing atmosphere at recent matches.

In ninth are Southampton, with St Mary's one of the larger stadiums in this season's Championship and often full to the brim with home supporters.

Those on the South Coast have also seen their loyalty tested in recent times after two relegations from the Premier League in three years, the latter of which saw them win just one home game all season.

Saints supporters also saw their club heavily criticised over the recent spygate scandal, but this has only added to the atmosphere on matchdays, particularly if those from the away end are quick to 'taunt' their rival fans for such misdemeanours.

Norwich City's home crowd at Carrow Road may not be the most hostile, but it is extremely hard to knock the fact that Norfolk's only professional club continues to attract such strong crowds despite how easy it could be for some locals to follow clubs outside the region.

The Canaries have endured extremely mixed starts in each of the past two seasons, with it even looking as though relegation to League One might have been possible at one stage.

Despite the club's fluctuating fortunes, you have to go back 22 years to find the last time average attendance figures dropped below the 20,000 mark in this part of the world.

Portsmouth's home crowd at Fratton Park is seventh on this list, with the historic ground still retaining plenty of character and a strong atmosphere to boot.

Despite being the fifth-smallest ground in the Championship this season, there have been less than 1,000 empty seats on average, and throughout John Mousinho's tenure, his side have accumulated plenty of points on home turf.

It was even claimed once by AC Milan and Brazil icon, Ronaldinho, that Pompey fans generated "the best atmosphere in world football," which is high praise indeed.

Millwall are next up on this list, with the hostile atmosphere at the Den well-documented throughout generations of football supporters.

The Lions home crowd is amongst the most raucous in English football despite the fact their stadium is the fourth-smallest by capacity in the Championship, and many were hoping to see such an atmosphere in the Premier League this term before Alex Neil's side fell short in the 2025/26 play-offs.

Again, a core of the club's supporters will turn up to SE16 regardless of the club's divisional status, with the best atmosphere undoubtedly being in the Dockers derby against West Ham United.

Which is the best home atmosphere you have ever experienced in the EFL? Comment below!

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2123. Michael O’Neill makes revelation over Terry Devlin’s Portsmouth future which will leave Championship rivals ‘disappointed’

Portsmouth have enjoyed a fine season to date, and versatile star Terry Devlin has been a standout player for John Mousinho’s side. Mainly playing at right-back, the 23-year-old has chipped in with four goals in 14 Championship games, including a brace in the 3-1 win over Swansea City at the start of November.

Devlin’s progression has brought interest from elsewhere, but Pompey have been working to secure his future at Fratton Park. Now, Northern Ireland boss Michael O’Neill has indicated that a positive conclusion is close. Speaking on the player’s situation with BBC Sport over the international break, he said: “He’s a very valuable player for Portsmouth.

“I think he’s in the process of signing a new contract there, and I imagine a lot of teams in the Championship will be disappointed by that.”

Devlin last extended his contract in February 2025 and he is tied down until 2028. He is in his fourth season with the South Coast outfit, having joined from Glentoran in the summer of 2023.

Tying Devlin down to a new deal marks a key move from Portsmouth. It secures his future before he enters the final 18 months of his current deal, but it also serves as a statement of intent to lock down one of their standout players and most valuable assets.

The 23-year-old has ups and downs over the course of his Pompey career but as a true utility player, he is a hugely valuable figure in Mousinho’s squad. His athleticism, attitude and well-rounded skillset means he can be trusted to deliver all over the pitch.

Furthermore, the deal will allow Devlin to stay focused on his own game. It will quieten noise over his future and a potential move elsewhere as ambitious sides like Wrexham have previously looked to prise him away from Fratton Park.

At 23, Devlin has time to grow on and off the pitch. On his current trajectory, his value will only grow, so Pompey will be glad to have him tied down to a secure and longer contract.

As touched on before, Devlin has been the subject of interest from other clubs previously. Those admirers will have been keeping a close eye on his situation with 18 months left on his deal.

However, on a new long-term deal, Portsmouth will be in a better place to stand firm on their valuation. If someone wants to buy him, they will have to pay a handsome fee to do so.

It doesn’t rule out interest or bids, especially if he keeps progressing as he has done, but Devlin’s future at Portsmouth will be far more certain if a new long-term contract is in place.

#2122. La Serie C non ha bisogno di Ronaldinho

Il ciclone Ronaldinho è passato. Cosa ci lascia in eredità? Dal punto di vista calcistico qualche colpo degno del suo repertorio di straordinario fuoriclasse e un contributo alla vittoria del Ravenna contro il Forlì. Poi, c'é tutto il resto. Un cocktail di curiosità, emozioni, voglia di fermare il tempo. Il derby di Romagna è stato un piccolo evento come dimostrano le montagne di titoli su qualsiasi organo di informazione e l'auditel della gara trasmessa da Sky. Se Ronaldinho doveva servire ad accendere i riflettori su un certo mondo la missione è perfettamente riuscita.

Ora che si sono spente le luci resta in piedi una domanda: il fuoriclasse brasiliano serve alla crescita della Serie C? Tra l'altro Ronaldinho nel chiudere per il momento questa esperienza ha lasciato la porta aperta alla possibilità di ritornare in Italia se il Ravenna fosse interessato a rivederlo in campo con la maglia giallorossa. Non so quale sarà la decisione dei dirigenti romagnoli. Penso però che Ronaldinho debba essere vissuto come un momento unico, da non ripetere. Il Ravenna non ha bisogno dei colpi, a tempo limitato, di questo fenomeno che non riesce a staccarsi dal pallone. E' una squadra forte, con alle spalle una società forte. I romagnoli hanno tutte le carte in regola per vincere il loro girone e conquistare la promozione in Serie B senza dover passare dalla lotteria dei play-off.

La Serie C, con l'ottimo presidente Marani, sta portando avanti battaglie più profonde. Nel nome di Gianfranco Zola sta cercando di diventare il palcoscenico ideale per la crescita di giovani talenti italiani. Quelli di cui abbiamo tutti un bisogno disperato a cominciare dal commissario tecnico Mancini. Salutato Ronaldinho con un applauso torniamo a lavorare in questa direzione. Chiedendo alle società di avere coraggio con i nostri talenti. La Serie C deve vivere nel futuro e non nel passato
