#2121. Bolton Wanderers fans will love what James Trafford said after England heroics v Spain

England became the first team to beat Spain since March 2024 on Sunday night, topping Group C of the Nations League, due in no small part to Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford. But even that double save at the end doesn't top one effort while at Bolton Wanderers.

The Three Lions weathered quite the storm in the final half hour, despite cruising at 3-0 thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Esri Konsa and Ben White.

A lapse in concentration let Lamine Yamal nick the ball and race away, and a second error seconds later saw Elliot Anderson drag the Spaniard down in the box, giving away a penalty and earning a straight red.

But despite Spain halving the deficit after converting the spot kick, England saw out the win, with Trafford proving to be the hero between the sticks. He made six saves, including a brilliant double stop at the end to deny Yamal and then Aymeric Laporte.

An incredible moment, and one that, for 99% of goalkeepers, would be the pinnacle of their careers thus far. Not for Trafford, though.

Trafford first made a name for himself as one of England's most exciting young goalkeepers while on loan at Bolton from Manchester City. He spent the second half of the 2021/22 campaign at the Toughsheet Stadium, but really broke through the following year.

The 24-year-old kept 22 clean sheets for the Trotters en route to the play-offs, making plenty of big saves to help what was then Ian Evatt's side save points, while also failing to concede in any of his four EFL Trophy matches as Bolton won at Wembley against Plymouth Argyle.

His second clean sheet back in a Wanderers shirt came at Port Vale, and despite it being over four years ago, he hasn't seemed to forget it.

FLW has debated which 15 fanbases generate the best atmospheres and more inside their home stadiums

Speaking to ITV after the win over Spain, Trafford was asked if that double save to deny Yamal and Laporte was "as good as he's made," and after thinking about it, the 24-year-old had to disagree.

"The moment's a brilliant moment," he said. "As in saves, I made an incredible one away at Port Vale when I was at Bolton, and that will forever be my best save. But for the moment, what it meant, yeah, it's up there."

The game ended 0-0 at Vale Park, and you'll be hard-pressed to find a fan of either side who remembers much about what happened, but that one moment will live in the goalkeeper's head for the rest of his career.

It's the old moniker, 'never fall in love with a loan player,' but it seems that the love is still mutual between Trafford and Bolton, even though his departure was over three years ago now.

As seen above, it's quite a brilliant save, and while Trafford and the Bolton fans had some brilliant memories after that third game of the campaign at Port Vale, those in the stands at the Toughsheet will love their mention after one of the best performances of the 24-year-old's life.

"I made an incredible [save] away at Port Vale when I was at Bolton" Our boy 🤍 we love you," one Bolton fan commented under the interview online. "Our boy james Trafford, loves Bolton and Bolton love him !!" was also among the comments, as was "He loves bolton . He always does."

"Makes a world-class double save to help England beat the world champions, but still puts another above it - Bolton away at Port Vale in League One. Never change!" a Bolton fan account tweeted.

"Hahahaha I love him England vs Spain? Yeah big moment, but fav save? For Bolton vs Port Vale 😂," was also commented. Trafford's matter-of-fact and somewhat unconventional interview style does lend well to some fans, especially those at Bolton, who will have immense pride towards their former loanee keeper.

Trafford is one of the prime examples of how EFL loans can help shape a player and ready them for big things in their career. The fact that the 24-year-old was playing in League One just four seasons ago is quite something.

Now, the Leeds number one is arguably one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League, and after that performance against Spain, the number one elect for England, according to some fans.

What current English EFL loanees do you think will make the step up into England contention in the future? Let us know in the comments.

A club's fanbase can often take pride in a former loanee going on to big things and, in this case, Bolton fans won't be letting the footballing world forget that Trafford was in their squad not that long ago.

From this, though, it seems that the 24-year-old himself isn't going to let people forget his time at the Toughsheet Stadium, either.

#2120. GdS: Club Brugge name price for Tresoldi – why a difficult negotiation beckons for Milan

AC Milan have already discovered the starting price for Nicolo Tresoldi, and it’s safe to say it will not be a cheap deal.

According to this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), it is no secret that Tresoldi sits at the top of the wish list for Milan. Gerry Cardinale, first and foremost, is a big admirer of the rising Brugge star.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is equally well-known that the striker has been a lifelong fan of the Rossoneri. However, his contract runs until 2029, so to take him away from the Jan Breydel Stadium a negotiation is needed with a club that are tough to deal with, as the past shows.

The phone lines between Milan and Brugge were first used in 2022, when the Charles De Ketelaere saga took place. Since then, the management teams at both Milan and the Belgian club have changed, but the history between the two sides should help facilitate discussions. Ardon Jashari was another arduous negotiation, but one that eventually reached the finish line too.

In the cases of De Ketelaere and Jashari, the pitch has arguably favoured the seller more than the buyer. Perhaps the outcome will be different with Tresoldi, should the two parties actually sit down to negotiate.

One caveat: especially in January, the asking is bound to be significant. How significant? Around €60m, according to whispers from Flanders.

Club Brugge are accustomed to selling their best players when the time comes, but they are under no pressure to do so, especially while the season is still underway. Tresoldi has effectively carried the team on his back, scoring eight goals in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Super Cup.

The total: 14 goals in 17 official matches. For the club to part ways with their star striker during the mid-season window – a time when all their competitive objectives remain within reach – the offer would certainly need to be more than substantial.

Furthermore, if the 22-year-old forward maintains his current scoring rate throughout the season, his market value will only continue to climb. It is a risk, but also an opportunity. Moreover, Milan are not alone in the race for Tresoldi.

Bayern Munich and top English clubs are keeping a close eye on the former Hannover man, who was born in Cagliari but is a key player for the German U21 national team. Consequently, if Cardinale wishes to beat the competition, he would need to act quickly and decisively.

🎬 Nicolò Tresoldi 🔴⚫️ https://t.co/tDcsnRgXiM

— AngelRedblack- MX #MilanSpace ❤🔴⚫ (@Angelredblack1) November 11, 2026

He demonstrated he can dothis over the summer with the signings of Gonçalo Ramos, Diego Moreira, and Mario Gila. However, authorising a €60m expenditure would require the right conditions: specifically, Milan must be in the hunt for a major objective.

Meanwhile, Tresoldi’s hat-trick against Inter at San Siro on October 13th in the Champions League has naturally excited the Rossoneri fans, who would be more than happy to embrace him. However, they aren’t the ones who have to pay the €60m.

#2119. Why fresh £70m Middlesbrough update will spark interest at Blackburn Rovers

The end of the calendar year is approaching, which means so is the January transfer window, and Championship clubs will be bracing for interest in some of the better-performing players in the division.

All eyes are on Middlesbrough at the moment, and how much interest they'll face for Will Lankshear, who only just joined the Teessiders this past summer in a deal which could break their transfer record.

As it stands, that potential £20 million fee may not be fully paid, as the 21-year-old has showcased his Premier League quality in the few months he's spent at the Riverside, and his potential is something that elite top-flight sides are keen to invest in.

Middlesbrough will be doing their best to scare off any potential suitors this January with a hefty price tag, but in the wake of their reported asking price, it raises the question of how much other clubs should demand for their big-hitters; more specifically, how much Blackburn Rovers should demand for Andri Gudjohnsen.

There was plenty of expectation surrounding Lankshear ahead of this season. The 21-year-old was still very highly rated out of the Tottenham Hotspur academy, hitting headlines after he scored and then was sent off in a Europa League defeat at Galatasaray in November 2024.

He'd also scored 12 in all competitions last year for an Oxford United side that was relegated from the Championship, with it almost universally agreed that he was a big bright spark in an otherwise disappointing campaign for the Yellows.

However, not many expected Lankshear to be this good, this soon, at his new club. The 21-year-old has 15 goals in 16 games in all competitions for Boro, including 13 in 13 Championship games.

The Middlesbrough frontman has been the clinical focal point that Kim Hellberg needed in his side, and it's evident through their lack of goals after he picked up a small hamstring issue how important he is to this Boro side.

Due to these performances, though, the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United and other Premier League sides are reportedly keen on his services as soon as this January. In response, the Sun reported that Middlesbrough have slapped a £70 million price tag on his head.

He wouldn't be the most expensive Championship departure if that did go through - West Ham United somehow managed to get £85 million for Mateus Fernandes this past summer - but it's an eyebrow-raising demand, and an equal indication that Lankshear is not for sale without blatantly outlining that.

Blackburn may be looking at the news regarding Middlesbrough's price tag for Lankshear and wonder why they can't adopt a similar approach as and when interest forms for their talisman, Andri Gudjohnsen.

Of the players who have played 750 minutes or more in the Championship this season, Lankshear and Gudjohnsen stand atop the goals-per-90 charts. The Boro man averages 1.12, while the Icelandic forward sits at 0.96. There's a sizable drop to Jack Moylan in third with 0.70.

Which fanbases can improve on their current atmosphere offerings? The computer has had its say....

Unlike the 21-year-old, though, Gudjohnsen hasn't needed a plethora of chances to score his goals, as Blackburn don't have the quality behind the striker as Middlesbrough does. Indeed, Lankshear has taken 28 more shots — more than double the Rovers man so far this season.

Gudjohnsen stands out due to his sheer prolific nature infront of goal. He has 10 this season from just 20 shots; a 50% conversion rate, which makes him the most clinical player in Europe.

Lankshear is important to Middlesbrough, but, arguably, Gudjohnsen at this stage is more crucial to Blackburn. If clubs come calling in January, Rovers need to be firm with their demands for the 24-year-old.

Ultimately, Middlesbrough's demands when it comes to a fee for Lankshear are heavily influenced by 'English tax.' English clubs always demand that little bit more, or in this case, a lot more, for home-grown domestic players.

Gudjohnsen isn't that, but instead, he comes with a marketable name that not many in his position have.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Arrow keys or WASD to move. P to pause, M to mute.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

The 24-year-old is a third-generation star, and both his grandfather and father were legends in Icelandic football. His Dad, Eidur, made quite a name for himself in England and Spain, too, winning a couple of Premier League titles with Chelsea and being part of the treble-winning Barcelona side under Pep Guardiola in 2008/09.

That kind of heritage is incredibly marketable. It'll make Icelandic fans follow their club and will draw eyes towards them to see how an Icelandic legend's son is performing in a big Premier League side.

Blackburn can use the Gudjohnsen name to their advantage to add a few more millions to the price tag to almost counteract the lack of homegrown status.

Ultimately, that £70 million price tag for Lankshear is a way to scare off suitors, and Blackburn should be doing the same. They aren't under any pressure to sell Gudjohnsen, given he signed a new "long-term" deal just last May.

How much do you think Andri Gudjohnsen is worth right now? Let us know in the comments.

The 24-year-old has showcased that this club form isn't just a fluke, netting a hat-trick for Iceland in their Nations League win over Bulgaria last Friday, and will return to Ewood Park looking to continue this momentum.

If he maintains this clinical nature in front of goal, Rovers could emerge as late play-off contenders as the campaign goes on. At the very least, it will attract further suitors in the summer, and Gudjohnsen's price tag could be even higher by then.

It may not be as lucrative as a £70 million fee, but Blackburn should be getting a little excited over how much they could earn from a Gudjohnsen sale in the future.

#2118. AC Milan among European sides keen on 17-year-old QPR breakout star

QPR have made a fine start to this season and currently occupy the final Championship play-off spot. The likes of Pierce Charles and Ronnie Edwards have earned the plaudits, while Richard Kone is finding his form again in attack, but a real breakout star has been 17-year-old Leon Scarlett.

Scarlett joined the club from Arsenal in April 2025, and so far this season he has made six appearances and clubs are starting to notice. Anthony Joseph has said that European giant AC Milan are tracking his progress after his start to the campaign.

The Italian side are not the only side keen, with Eintracht Frankfurt also keeping tabs on Scarlett’s situation. Both sides have expressed interest in the winger, who is already a Wales under-21 international.

QPR youngster Scarlett is attracting growing attention after breaking into Julien Stephan’s first-team plans this season, with AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt reportedly monitoring his progress.

The 17-year-old Welsh winger joined QPR in January 2025 after spending around a decade in Arsenal’s academy, having been released by the Gunners. Primarily operating on the left, Scarlett is known for his explosive acceleration, close control and ability to beat defenders in one-on-one situations.

He made his senior debut aged 16 in May 2026 and has featured regularly from the bench, but he did start against Preston back in September, accumulating around 130 minutes. He has also represented Wales at multiple youth levels, including the U21s.

Manager Stephan has praised his personality and willingness to express himself in first-team training, with QPR viewing him as an exciting prospect. He is playing ahead of his age right now and QPR fans have every right to be excited about Scarlett’s potential.

QPR must resist interest from AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt in Scarlett, with the 17-year-old better off continuing his development at Loftus Road.

Scarlett has enjoyed a rapid rise since leaving Arsenal’s academy, earning first-team opportunities under Stephan. However, with only around 130 Championship minutes to his name and no senior goal or assist yet, a move abroad would arguably come too soon.

Stephan has a proven record of developing young talent, while QPR are placing increasing emphasis on their academy pathway. Scarlett’s explosive pace, close control and ability to beat defenders make him an exciting prospect, but he needs regular exposure to senior football to refine his game.

A move to Milan or Frankfurt could leave him fighting for opportunities in youth sides rather than progressing at first-team level. QPR should keep hold of Scarlett, gradually increase his involvement and allow his performances and value to grow before considering a big-money departure.

#2116. Ibrahimovic shares feelings on ‘bond’ with Milan: “The most important team in my life”

Zlatan Ibrahimovic has shed light on just how much AC Milan mean to him, labelling it the ‘most important’ club he has represented.

Today marks the launch of ‘Il Milan nel Mondo’, Mauro Suma’s new book exploring the Rossoneri’s reach beyond both Milan and Italy. Several Rossoneri Legends will join the author at the launch this morning, including Daniele Massaro, Demetrio Albertini and Filippo Galli.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ibrahimovic wrote a foreword in the book, which has been relayed by MilanNews. The RedBird Capital senior advisor spoke about just how much the club means to him, after his two spells as a player and now his time as an executive.

“Milan are the most important team in my life. And it’s also the only one that convinced me to return. In my career, I’ve worn legendary shirts, played in wonderful cities, and won everywhere. But Milan was something different,” he said.

“It was the only club that truly drew me back, the only one where I felt the need to start over. Convincing Zlatan to return isn’t easy. It’s not easy for anyone. Yet, with Milan, it’s happened more than once.

“This means that between me and these colours, a bond has been created that goes beyond football, beyond trophies, even beyond time. Victory remains in the halls of fame; some teams, however, stay with you. AC Milan belongs to this category.

“The first time, AC Milan brought me happiness, the second, love. In the Rossoneri, I found a sense of belonging that is increasingly rare in modern football. Because starting an adventure with a club can happen. Returning a second time, and then again, means that the club and its fans have become part of you.

“AC Milan are the most successful Italian club at international level, but it’s not just a collection of trophies. It’s an identity. It’s a way of being in football and in the world. Wherever it goes, it leaves a mark. And those who join AC Milan, sometimes, never leave.”

Ibrahimovic signed the first time in August 2010 after an experience at Barcelona that wasn’t a positive one, and he helped Milan to the Scudetto with a 14-goal haul. He won the Capocannoniere the next season, doubling that tally.

He returned in 2019 and scored 25 goals in 37 appearances in his first two campaigns, securing a return to European competitions. At the end of his third season, the climb was complete: the Rossoneri won their 19th league title.

Then, in June 2023 came his emotional farewell at San Siro, before Zlatan returned to the club but wearing a suit and tie.

#2115. Top 8 most famous footballers to ever play in the EFL Championship (Ranked)

The Championship is a fantastic league when it comes to producing talent, with many of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad having featured at this level in the past.

The competitive nature of the second tier, combined with the technical and physical demands it places on players, mean it’s a relentless division that will test individuals in different ways.

Some struggle to cope with that, although others flourish, and it can be the perfect environment for young players to show what they can do.

However, it’s not just up-and-coming players who enjoy the Championship, as some of the biggest names in the game have turned out in England’s second division in the past.

Football League World has asked AI to predict the 2027/28 EFL Championship table if Manchester United and Manchester City were in it

With that in mind, FLW has ranked the EIGHT most famous footballers to have played in the Championship, even if they weren’t necessarily the best…

The 39-year-old is a Leicester City legend, with the high point of his career coming when he helped the Foxes to the Premier League title.

Many people love Vardy for his rise to the top, which saw him make the jump from non-league Fleetwood Town to Leicester when they were in the Championship, and it was a move that kickstarted his career, which would eventually make him a household name.

Vardy is still playing in the Championship right now, turning out for Burnley, and is undoubtedly one of the most famous names in the league.

Walker is a teammate of Vardy’s at Turf Moor, and he is a player who has enjoyed a glittering career at the highest level.

During his time with Man City, the right-back won six Premier League titles, a Champions League and numerous domestic trophies. Walker was integral to City’s success under Pep Guardiola, and is in the discussion as the best right-back the league has seen.

When you add in 96 England caps, Walker has had a remarkable career, which started with Sheffield United in the Championship.

Many people consider Cole as the best left-back England have ever had, with the Arsenal academy graduate winning over 100 caps for the Three Lions, which is a fantastic achievement.

During his club career with the Gunners and Chelsea, Cole won every honour possible, which included lifting the Champions League with the Blues after beating Bayern Munich on their own patch in 2012.

Cole was a superb one-vs-one defender, and whilst he spent the majority of his career at the top, he ended up at Derby County, and whilst he didn’t make a huge impact at Pride Park, having a player of that calibre at the club would’ve benefited the younger players.

Bellingham is one of the most famous footballers on the planet right now, with the midfielder starring for Real Madrid and England.

But, it all started for the Stourbridge-born Bellingham at Birmingham City, who are a club that are still close to his heart. He broke through at Blues as a 16-year-old, and it became apparent very quickly that they had a special talent on their hands.

At 23, Bellingham still has so much more to offer, and there’s every chance that he could go on to become the most famous footballer on this list, as he will fancy his chances of winning the Ballon d’Or, as well as aiming for more success with Real Madrid, and leading England to a major trophy.

Terry is another Premier League legend, with the defender among the best centre-backs to have played at the top level in English football during his time with Chelsea.

He won five Premier League titles, five FA Cups, three League Cups and a Champions League in a brilliant career, with Terry also representing England 78 times, many of which were as captain.

Even though Terry is associated with Chelsea, he ended his playing career at Aston Villa in the Championship, with his final game a play-off final loss to Fulham at Wembley.

Bale is a legend of Welsh football, having been the driving force behind what has been their best period in the past decade, where they qualified for major tournaments and reached the semi-final of Euro 2016.

On the club stage, Bale was part of a Real Madrid team that dominated in Europe, and he ended his career having won the Champions League five times, which is an outstanding achievement.

It all started for Bale with Southampton, though, where he had one full breakout season before joining Spurs.

The ex-Man Utd forward is one of the best players that England have produced, and he is another player on the list that won every honour available during his club career.

Rooney also won 120 caps for England, and he was the Three Lions’ record goalscorer before he was beaten by Harry Kane, so he was a key figure for both club and country for the chunk of his time as a player.

The attacker was another player who ended his career in the Championship, with Rooney joining Derby County under Phillip Cocu, who he would then replace as head coach, to give him his first taste of management.

Who is the most famous footballer you've seen in the Championship? Let us know in the comments below.

Kane may not have the trophy cabinet of many on this list, but as the only Ballon d’Or winner, we feel he has to go in as number one.

The striker is the all-time England record goalscorer and appearance maker, and he is now picking up silverware on a regular basis with Bayern Munich, having undoubtedly established himself as one of the best players in the world in the past few years.

That recognition as number one on the planet arrived earlier this year, and it capped off an incredible journey for Kane, who turned out for Millwall and Leicester in the Championship during loan spells earlier in his career, and for Leyton Orient in League One.

#2114. League One clubs target Linfield winger amid impressive form

Rhys Brennan’s form has attracted the attention of League One sides, who face competition from teams in the SPL. At this moment in time, none of the admirers are named in O’Rourke’s report.

Brennan, 20, is predominantly a right winger. He is out on loan with Linfield away from Bohemian, where his contract runs out next December.

Bohemian currently sit 3nd in the Irish Premier Division, whilst Linfield top the Northern Irish Premiership, having won 12 of their 16 matches so far. Brennan has contributed well to their success, locking down a starting berth on the flanks.

Brennan broke into the Bohemian side in 2025 and has since developed on loan at Cobh Ramblers before Linfield. A move to England would constitute a major step in Rhys Brennan’s career, should it take place.

Brennan’s debut for Bohemian came against Waterford at the end of the 2024 campaign. He soon followed that up with a first goal the following Monday, scoring as his side overturned a 2-0 deficit to win 3-2 against Shamrock Rovers.

Brennan has also featured for the Republic of Ireland U19s. The winger made his debut for the side away against Slovakia in a 3-1 friendly victory back in March 2024.

The young winger is an energetic presence on the wing. He’s shown he can offer a dual threat of goals and assists, but his crossing ability and work rate is where he stands out.

Furthermore, Brennan is a confident presence on the wing. He leads the way for Linfield with regard to successful dribbles per match this season, averaging 1.9 successful dribbles per 90.

This season is the first season where Brennan is fully flourishing in senior football. Should he make the move to England, he might need time to adapt given the step up from Northern Ireland to League One.

Brennan will not walk into a side challenging for promotion and integrate himself with regular minutes. Equally, a relegation battle would not be beneficial for his career.

A move to a mid-table side seems safe, giving Brennan a low pressure environment to develop and express himself on the wings.

Linfield will be reluctant to lose Rhys Brennan this season. However, should the player’s form continue, he may be a serious candidate for a move in the January transfer window, and a decision will ultimately be made by his parent club Bohemian.

#2113. Bradford City takeover: Everything we know right now

Bradford City are being linked to a potential takeover by a Thai-based consortium, so here's a round-up of the latest on whether this move might come off.

The international break couldn't have come at a better time for Bradford City.

Following an exceptional start to the season, the departure of manager Graham Alexander to Preston North End at the start of October hit the club hard, and they went into the break with just one win from their last six league matches and having slipped from the top of the League One table to eighth place, having replaced Alexander with the former Wycombe Wanderers manager Michael Duff.

But losing Alexander may not even be the biggest change to be coming to Bradford City this season. It's been rumoured that a Thai-based consortium are considering launching a bid to buy the club from current owner Stefan Rupp, with the group having been attracted by the club's recent upward trajectory and potential, given the size of attendances they were attracting, even while the team was misfiring in League Two.

This isn't the first time since Rupp purchased the club in 2016 that there has been an attempt to wrest Bradford City from his control, so here's a round-up of what's been said about ongoing reported interest in buying them, and what it could mean for a club who previously slipped from the Premier League to League Two in just six years, between 2001 and 2007.

A report from journalist Alan Nixon on Sunday morning has reopened conjecture that the Bradford City owner Stefan Rupp could be set to sell the club after ten years of ownership. Nixon confirmed on his Patreon that "Bradford City are a surprise target for a Thai-based group" who have been considering buying into the EFL.

Nixon confirmed that the prospective bidders have shown interest in buying a club before, and that, "Bradford could be for sale at the right price and the Thais, who have an intermediary with inside knowledge, are considering an official offer."

Do you think Bradford City would be better off under new ownership? Let us know in the comments below!

But before anything else, any new owners will have to get a takeover past Rupp, and that might not be completely straightforward. The German has been reported to be more open to selling since the club were promoted from League Two in 2025, with The Athletic's Matt Slater reporting in March 2026 that, "Rupp has been listening to offers for years but has showing a bit more leg ever since last season’s promotion."

Rupp has, however, said in the past that he won't sell up to just anybody. In 2021, he rejected an offer from the US cryptocurrency investors WAGMI United. They instead turned their attention to Crawley Town but, since completing their takeover of the Sussex-based club in April 2022, Crawley's position has waned considerably, with the Red Devils currently propping up the rest of the EFL and six points from safety.

Rumours that Bradford City could be sold have provoked a strong reaction from fans of the club, so here's a selection of what they've had to say.

This poll of fans showed a majority of those who voted being against any takeover of their club:

While this fan doesn't believe that these rumours should be a surprise to anybody:

This fan is concerned over what's happened at several other clubs who've come under far eastern ownership:

And this fan believes that Stefan Rupp has already demonstrated that he is the owner that Bradford City need:

Their recent slump in League One notwithstanding, the direction of travel that Bradford City have undertaken over the last couple of seasons makes them a prime target for those seeking to buy into the English game.

For years, it felt as though the Bantams had everything bar the team. They had a stadium which is fit for Premier League football, and attendances were extremely healthy, even when the team wasn't performing especially well in League Two. On top of this, being the only professional football club in a city of half a million people gives the opportunity for further growth, should they continue to rise through the divisions.

Under Alexander, the team was finally successful, winning promotion back to League One in 2025 following an absence of six years, and their first season back hinted that the Bantams weren't done either, with the team finishing in a highly creditable fourth place before losing 2-0 on aggregate to Bolton Wanderers in the semi-finals of the play-offs.

But there is one word in Alan Nixon's report which may cause Bradford fans to worry a little about the nature of the group who are now being linked with the club. Nixon described this consortium as "speculators", and that will raise concerns about the motives of this group among some.

There isn't anywhere near enough detail about this group to be able to draw too many inferences about their intentions for the club, though it's previously been reported that they are connected to the former owners of Oxford United. But "speculators" is a loaded word, and there may be concern over whether they will have their own interests at heart or those of the club should they take over.

And when speaking to the Bradford Telegraph & Argus at the end of June, Rupp confirmed that, "You get requests from time to time but they are tyre kickers, people without money, wannabe football club owners, or people you simply don't like," and that, "I'm the keeper of the keys and I would never hand it over to somebody where I have the impression he can't do any better."

The sale price, should it be the same as it was reported to be earlier in 2026, would be unlikely to be too much of a sticking point. The Athletic's report in March suggested that £10 million could be enough to persuade him to sell, with Bradford owning neither their own ground nor their training ground, but such a sum could still only be considered a drop in the ocean, were the club to ascend to the Championship or beyond.

Still in the FA Cup, and with an EFL Cup quarter-final at Manchester City to look forward to in the middle of December, Bradford City remain in a better condition on the pitch than they have been for years, and the big irony of their current position is that this very success may push up their sale price. Stefan Rupp has said before that he will only sell the club to the right buyer, but the true test of his principles may come when the rumours cease and concrete offers start to land on his desk.

#2111. Bristol City and Bristol Rovers fans both face the same issue right now

The two Bristol clubs don't meet often, yet their rivalry is one of the fiercest in the English game. Right now, though, City and Rovers fans are united in their dislike of their current managers.

We're right in the midst of sacking season in the EFL, and both Michael Skubala and Steve Evans are edging closer to the trapdoor, having failed thus far, with both sides having lofted expectations ahead of the campaign.

Bristol City have had those expectations since their run to the play-offs under Liam Manning in 2024/25, but a transfer window which saw plenty of investment into the playing squad, with the likes of Dom Ballard, Lorent Tolaj, Lisav Eissat and others arriving, has only stoked that anticipation that they could make a run towards the top eight.

Meanwhile, all the good feeling that Steve Evans created in the latter stages of last season and in the first few weeks of this year has dissipated, with the Gas routinely beaten and looking over their shoulders, which wasn't the plan at all this year.

While Bristol City fans would like to have maintained their play-off level in the last couple of years, there was some potential leeway regarding some form of a project over the summer.

The Robins had a little shake-up in the board over the past year, with Charlie Boss appointed CEO in February, a few months after lifelong fan Richard Scudamore became a member of the board and Sporting Director James Ellis arrived this past summer. This is their first full season at the club.

Bringing in Michael Skubala and investing in some promising players from League One and abroad indicated that this would be a multi-year project to try and get into the Premier League, but as it stands, Bristol City are sleepwalking towards the third tier, winning just two of their last 10 games.

More importantly, though, Skubala's brand of football isn't giving fans the belief that things will get better. They've scored just four goals at Ashton Gate, and lost their last home game 5-0 against Norwich City. To many, that was the final straw.

Evidently, Robins fans aren't having Skubala in charge anymore, and once you lose the supporters, it's hard to see a route back.

While Michael Skubala's situation is very much a project yet to get going, the fall-off at Bristol Rovers for Steve Evans these last couple of months has been head-scratching and rather alarming.

It was just six months ago that Evans was celebrating amongst the fans in their 4-0 win over Cheltenham Town, marking their seventh successive victory at the Memorial Ground and their eighth straight in league action. If he went into the crowd now, they'd probably have a different reaction.

The Gas were many's pre-season favourites in League Two this year after they ended last season with 11 wins in their final 14 games, and they started this term with four wins from five. Since then, it's been one win and eight defeats in 10.

The credit that Evans built up through the latter stages of last season has left the bank, and Gas fans are calling for a change.

Saturday's home defeat against Chesterfield leaves Bristol Rovers sitting 18th in League Two, with the main concerns coming from the effort of the players during this dry spell of form.

Bristol City made their decision over the international break. With fans calling for Michael Skubala's head, CEO Charlie Boss sent a message of confidence towards their head coach.

Regardless of what Robins fans think, there can be some admiration that the hierarchy hasn't panicked immediately and is willing to give Skubala time to try and turn the ship around and oversee the multi-year project he signed up for in the summer.

FLW ranks the eight most famous footballers to have played in the Championship at some point in their career.

The schedule doesn't get any easier for Bristol City after the break, though, with Middlesbrough, Wrexham, West Brom and Swansea City coming up in their next four games.

City fans are going to have to stick with Skubala through this difficult period and try to will their side on to collect some points. If not, the Robins could be in a relegation battle as we head towards Christmas, and a sacking then would only be seen as a decision made weeks too late at Ashton Gate.

While there hasn't been a direct vote of confidence at board level, Steve Evans may still have a small amount of credit left to try and turn this dreadful form around at the Memorial Stadium.

Evans' predecessor, Darrell Clarke, was sacked after losing 10 straight league games, so the higher-ups have shown patience where it may have been running thin in the stands previously.

Do you think both Michael Skubala and Steve Evans will be in their respective jobs by 2027? Let us know in the comments.

There's also the possibility that things don't get better without Evans in the dugout, who has achieved success nearly everywhere he's been, especially in League Two, with him getting Rotherham United and Stevenage promoted from this level in the past.

Right now, both sets of fans in Bristol want their current head coaches to leave, but it doesn't seem like that will happen anytime soon. Only time will tell whether those decisions are the correct ones.

#2109. Cardiff City & Swansea City face joint Grimsby Town transfer cringe right now

Cardiff City, Swansea City, Grimsby Town, and Iwan Morgan are all enjoying rather different fortunes in the 2026/27 campaign, but there is an interesting connection between the three clubs.

The two South Wales rivals are back competing at the same level again and both have plenty of reasons to be optimistic about their respective seasons. Cardiff City are rebuilding impressively following their relegation, while Swansea City are beginning to look a far more competitive outfit.

Neither has yet had the chance to get one over their rivals in the league, but that will change at the end of November when they finally meet for their first Championship clash since 2024/25. There is, however, another story they might both be keeping an eye on.

Iwan Morgan looks like a serious star in the making at Grimsby Town, with the 20-year-old already establishing himself as one of the most exciting young attacking talents in the EFL for the League Two outfit. His latest goal involvements came via a brace against Swindon Town during a 4-1 away win on Saturday.

Having left Brentford over the summer, the forward has hit the ground running, registering five goals and five assists already this season. What makes his emergence particularly interesting is his previous involvement in the academies of both Cardiff and Swansea.

The 25 top scorers in the Championship since the second tier was rebranded back in 2004/05, including Billy Sharp and Aleksandar Mitrovic.

He left Swansea after three years there in 2023, joining Brentford. Prior to that, the Cardiff-born forward had been with the Bluebirds for nine years. Also, these are two clubs with excellent youth-development structures and a strong reputation for giving homegrown players opportunities to establish themselves in senior football.

Morgan could quite conceivably have been starring for either side by now, or at least featuring in some capacity, but instead he is making a name for himself at Grimsby. With his performances attracting attention, both Welsh rivals could soon be left wondering how such an exciting talent slipped through their fingers.

One of the biggest frustrations for clubs developing young players is that talent can sometimes be overlooked until somebody further down the football pyramid recognises its potential.

Youngsters can be loaned out to levels that do not necessarily reflect their ability, while others are allowed to leave without ever receiving a proper opportunity in senior football.

Morgan appears to be another example of a player who might have been ready for a greater challenge much sooner. His performances suggest he is already capable of operating at League One level at the very least, despite being only 20 and playing for a Grimsby side in League Two.

Cardiff and Swansea may have missed their opportunity, but Grimsby's gain is enormous. They have secured a player whose ceiling could be considerably higher than the level at which they currently compete. If he helps to fire them up, he could yet be a major asset in the third tier next season.

It is not as though either Cardiff or Swansea have been particularly poor in their recent recruitment strategies. Cardiff have rebuilt impressively following relegation, adding plenty of players under the age of 25 to an existing core of academy graduates who have already demonstrated considerable quality.

They now boast one of the youngest squads in the Championship, with a project that has genuine potential to develop further. Swansea, meanwhile, have turned to Jamestown Analytics to help shape their recruitment under Vitor Matos.

West Ham United headed into the international break not quite where they hoped they'd be, but the Hammers remain well and truly in automatic promotion contention, as new head coach Scott Parker sets his sights on improving the squad.

West Ham sit just outside of the play-off places as things stand after six wins, five draws, and four defeats in their opening 15 games upon their return to the Championship.

Amid the club's struggles, Nuno Espírito Santo was dismissed from his post in the London Stadium dugout, swiftly being replaced by former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker, who made 129 appearances for West Ham as a player once upon a time, knows exactly what the Hammers supporters demand, and having had the opportunity to assess his squad over the break, has outlined two key areas in need of improvement this winter.

According to Alan Nixon's Patreon, Parker has identified left-back and striker as the two areas West Ham must be targeting heading into the January window.

With Taty Castellanos, Pablo Felipe, and Joel Piroe as options up front right now, it's not exactly as if the Hammers are short on strength and depth in this area, but despite this, Parker is clearly not totally convinced by any of that trio as things stand.

At left-back, each of Ollie Scarles, Morato, Adam Boiro, and Ezra Mayers has covered this area of the pitch at some stage this season, though none have been able to successfully nail down a starting berth under either Nuno or Parker.

It would be no surprise to see West Ham splash the cash this winter once again to boost their promotion chances, and should look towards a fellow top-eight contender to strike a deal.

Between them, Castellanos, Pablo, and Piroe have six league goals so far this campaign, with the latter grabbing four of those, as neither Castellanos nor Pablo have been able to adapt to the Championship.

Vipotnik, 24, finished as the Championship's top goalscorer last season, with 23 goals and three assists in 44 league appearances for Swansea City, as midway through the season, the Hammers registered an interest in the forward.

Swansea would stand firm on Vipotnik, who would eventually sign a fresh deal in South Wales, but this season, he has found himself battling for minutes with Adam Idah and Ross Stewart, as a move this winter could be on the cards.

Although Vipotnik has fallen down the pecking order at Swansea this season, his goalscoring ability at this level is undeniable, and West Ham must be looking to take advantage of his situation.

With Castellanos and Pablo likely to exit after their poor starts to the season, Vipotnik would offer a different option up top at the London Stadium, and a coach like Parker will know how to get the best out of him.

Tymon, since joining Swansea from Stoke in the summer of 2023, has cemented himself as one of the very best in his position in the entire division, especially going forward, with his excellent delivery proving incredibly difficult to defend against.

At 27 and with nearly 250 Championship appearances under his belt across his career, Tymon is in his prime years and knows the division better than most, as though neither will likely come especially cheap; if they can help guide the Hammers back to the Premier League, it would be difficult to deny they're worth it.

#2106. EFL clubs face uncertain future as Andy Burnham warns over major TV rule change

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged caution over scrapping the 3pm blackout, and EFL clubs may have good cause to back him over this.

With rates of the illegal streaming of matches continuing to rise, there has been much conjecture in recent times over whether it is time for the ending of the 3pm blackout for televised matches.

The blackout, which prevents the broadcasting of live matches from the Premier League and the Championship between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on a Saturday, has come in for increasing criticism in recent years from fans of clubs who are unable to legally watch matches between these times while their counterparts have the ability to do so.

But now an interjection from Prime Minister Andy Burnham has cast fresh doubt over whether the blackout will be lifted in the near future, after he explained that such a decision needs to be handled carefully in order to protect smaller clubs.

The BBC have reported that Prime Minister Andy Burnham saying that he is sceptical about the removal of the 3pm blackout. Burnham has said that he believes that any removal of the blackout should be handled extremely carefully in order to protect the revenues of smaller clubs.

Burnham has said that, "I would urge a bit of caution [on the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs," adding that, "If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league."

Do you think the 3pm blackout should remain, to protect smaller clubs? Let us know in the comments below!

Burnham, who is a long-standing supporter of Premier League club Everton, said that he wouldn't be taking a solely consumer-orientated view of removing the blackout: "I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health-of-football approach to this particular issue."

And he also confirmed that his main aim with regard to this issue is the protection of English football's unique pyramid system: "I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all."

Andy Burnham is actively considering scrapping the law that bans football fans from drinking in the stands

The 3pm blackout was first introduced in the 1960s, at a time when the televised coverage of football was first really starting to proliferate and the attitude of clubs towards the broadcasting of matches was very different to today.

At a time when match-day revenue was how clubs made the majority of their incomes, there was deep suspicion on the part of owners and chairmen about what sort of effect the widespread televising of matches might have on revenue coming into clubs.

An attempt to show live Football League matches had failed in 1960 after just one match was shown, but with England hosting a World Cup in 1966 there was increased interest from broadcasters in showing matches. The Burnley chairman Bob Lord spearheaded the opposition, which resulted in the blackout being introduced. Live televised football from the Football League didn't return until October 1983.

Critics of the blackout argue that it is a relic from a bygone age. In an era during which matches can be illegally streamed from elsewhere in the world, they argue that allowing all matches to be shown on the television regardless of kick-off times would be beneficial to clubs, who could charge more for their rights, and for fans of big clubs who want to see all of their teams' matches live.

The counter-argument to this is that, while no-one knows for sure what would happen were the blackout to be lifted, it's difficult to imagine a scenario in which it would be good for smaller clubs. Anecdotal evidence has long suggested that smaller clubs take a hit when they have matches scheduled for the same time as bigger matches.

And it remains the case that smaller EFL clubs and non-league clubs remain more dependent on match-day revenues than bigger clubs. This isn't to say that it doesn't matter to Premier League clubs, for whom it remains their third-largest source of income. But without television deals of the value of the Premier League's or vast commercial contracts, the lower you travel down the football pyramid, the more dependent clubs are on supporters turning out for matches. A YouGov poll in 2023 found that 14% of match-going fans would be more likely to stay at home in the event that matches were shown on the television at 3pm on a Saturday.

Furthermore, supporters of retaining the ban argue that removing the blackout would be akin to letting a genie out of a bottle. The likelihood of removing the ban would be a one-way street, and even if the effects of it were more severe for smaller clubs than anticipated, the likelihood of it being reinstated would be extremely thin. And with the rights to Premier League or Championship matches still being extremely valuable, big increases to the amounts being paid for matches at that level would only further widen the financial gap between the wealthiest clubs and the rest.

The Premier League and EFL could, if they wanted to, remove all of their matches from the period covered by the 3pm blackout and ensure that all matches could be shown live on the television. But with matches already routinely being shown at lunchtime, early in the evening, and increasingly on Saturday nights, it seems unlikely that the bigger clubs would do anything but fill in the gaps with more live televised football in the event that it was removed.

Andy Burnham's comments will cause a mixed reaction. The 2023 YouGov poll found that 25% of all fans supported the blackout while 52% were against it, though these numbers changed to 44% in favour and 45% against when it came to match-going fans. Balancing these opposing interests could prove tricky for the Prime Minister, given the conflicting nature of the desire of bigger clubs to maximise their revenues and smaller clubs' fears over what effect loosening or abolishing it could have upon them.

#2104. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2103. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2102. QPR face losing star that Jimmy Dunne called 'so impressive'

QPR have enjoyed uplifting progression under Julien Stephan into contention for a play-off place in the Championship this season, but the West Londoners may now be applying some focus to resisting the threat of transfer interest in one particular starlet from Italian giants AC Milan following fresh reports.

The Hoops have transitioned from mid-table mediocrity to Championship promotion hopefuls after completing what was widely felt to be an exciting summer transfer window, which included the arrivals of Pierce Charles, Dennis Cirkin, Glen Kamara and Tariq Lamptey.

As such, QPR find themselves positioned in eighth place amid the ongoing November international break and, having lost just two of their last ten matches against automatic promotion hopefuls in Birmingham City and Southampton, Stephan's outfit appear firmly capable of continuing to fight it out for a top-eight finish.

Away from the pitch, however, QPR are now facing a new worry as AC Milan and others hone in their transfer sights on one Loftus Road star who Stephan's players would certainly hate to see depart out of W12.

As reported by Sky Sports' Anthony Joseph on Monday afternoon, QPR prodigy Leon Scarlett is attracting interest from mainland Europe in a development that will leave Hoops supporters worried about losing the club's top young prospect.

Indeed, Joseph has claimed that both AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt have already expressed an interest in the highly-rated 17-year-old's services ahead of the looming January transfer window, with the continental pair reportedly continuing to monitor his situation at Loftus Road.

Scarlett, who has made six senior appearances for the second-tier play-off hopefuls to date since heading across London to join from Arsenal in January of last year, has enjoyed a meteoric rise and is regarded as a future star in the making.

The talented winger made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at Ipswich Town on the final day of the previous season before climbing up Stephan's ranks throughout the summer and appearing in current-campaign clashes against Charlton Athletic, West Bromwich Albion, Preston North End, Derby County and Birmingham.

Sunderland and Wolverhampton Wanderers were interested in Queens Park Rangers striker Rumarn Burrell in the summer

Scarlett has made quite the impression in some of those encounters, too, and while the ex-Arsenal academy starlet is yet to open his professional goalscoring account, QPR fans are desperate to see more appearances in the coming weeks and months.

That could change if either AC Milan or Frankfurt seal a swoop, though, with Scarlett's star only rising after collecting a pair of caps with Wales' U21 set-up for good measure.

Scarlett has earned rave reviews from supporters, players and coaches alike since being fast-tracked into Stephan's first-team fold, which is precisely why the R's will be eager to avoid losing such an exciting young asset.

Stephan, who knows a thing or two about developing top-grade talent after previously coaching world stars such as Eduardo Camavinga, 2025 Ballon D'Or winner Ousmane Dembele and Manchester City wing-king Jeremy Doku at Rennes, has already talked up Scarlett's quality.

The Frenchman has been keeping a close eye on the Welsh youth international's ever-accelerating development throughout the year, and was left impressed after promoting him to the senior squad in the closing stages of last term. Stephan told the Hounslow Herald: "The last game (Scarlett) did for the U21s, he did very well.

"I saw him in a cup game with the U18s earlier in the season and he did a good first half. So I just wanted to see him during the session with us (the first team). And during the session, he did well."

Scarlett has excited his teammates, too, with club captain Jimmy Dunne a notable example.

Speaking at a fans forum event back in September, the popular defender also explained: "Just watching Leon Scarlett today he’s so impressive, so bright, and so positive.

"You want to see him do well and thrive."

Only time will tell, of course, whether the likes of Dunne, Stephan and QPR as a whole can see Scarlett reach his full potential at Loftus Road and become the beneficiaries of the wide-man's talent and footballing ceiling - or if a larger European club will end up reaping the rewards instead.

It's clear that QPR could just need to implement some form of action in order to guarantee Scarlett's longer-term future, with the prodigious forward surely capable of becoming a first-team regular in the next twelve months.

The worry right now will be that Scarlett remains contracted to the scholarship deal he penned under two years ago to join from Arsenal, and can be easily poached until he agrees to sign professional terms.

QPR would surely love to put that sort of contract on the table for Scarlett, and will need to find out exactly where the player's own desires lie in light of emerging interest from a juggernaut of European football and one of the continent's premiere talent-developers in Frankfurt.

QPR fans, how do you feel about AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt's interest in Leon Scarlett? Are you worried that the exciting winger will leave Loftus Road for bigger things already? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Either way, the Championship side are susceptible to losing Scarlett before his Hoops career has really taken off, and it's no surprise that vultures are circling in an effort to exploit that situation and prize away the teenage prodigy.

#2101. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2100. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2097. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

Leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches.
